## assistant — 2026-08-20T14:09:23

`[V1-doc]`, `[V1.0]`, `[V1.1]`, `[V1.2]` are in **v2**, inserted right after `[WRAPPERS]` so the verification sits above the old R-series. Geometry dry-run passes for every plausible Λ (300–388 nm) and triad orientation.

## What V1 tests

**C23**: a lattice at Λ/2 spacing (sign period = Λ), 10 V × 1 s, charge-balanced, drives the local texture to the commanded director. Same recipe as C23 — nothing tuned.

The prediction is a **3 × 3 confusion matrix** of commanded against achieved direction, which should be diagonal. Three replicates of each of the three directors, all in one frame.

## Two design choices that come straight from R8's failure

**Latin square, not one direction per row.** Each director appears exactly once in every row and every column:

| | col 0 | col 1 | col 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| row 0 | d0 | d1 | d2 |
| row 1 | d1 | d2 | d0 |
| row 2 | d2 | d0 | d1 |

R8's untouched control drifted **+0.106** against a 0.029 floor. Had the directions been grouped by row, that drift would be indistinguishable from a row effect. With a Latin square any smooth gradient shifts all three commands equally, so **a diagonal matrix cannot be produced by drift**. That's what replaces the untouched panel — nine panels leave no room for one, and this is the stronger control anyway, because drift can't send neighbouring panels to *different* commanded directions. `[V1.0]` asserts the square is valid before building.

**Identical dose in every panel.** A lattice rotated by θ has its bounding box inflated by |cos θ|+|sin θ|, which varies up to 1.41× across the triad. Deriving `N_SIDE` per panel from a fixed box would give the three directions **different pulse counts** — dose confounded with direction, which would have quietly broken the whole verification. So `N_SIDE` is global (**64 pulses per panel**, 576 total at Λ = 388) and every panel is scored over the same core, sized to the *smallest* box (3.6 Λ).

## The guard that would have saved R8

`[V1.0]` measures the virgin peak and **stops** if it's more than 20° from the nearest director. R8 started at 91° — 29° and 31° from its neighbours — and wandered all session. This rejects a bad area in four minutes instead of fifty. It also warns if the floor comes out above 0.030.

Verified in the dry run: cores stay clear of neighbours' 625 nm halos (halo reaches 1.56 µm, neighbour core edge at 1.97 µm), everything inside the frame, ~27 min total.

## To run

1. `[TOOLKIT]` and `[WRAPPERS]` — v2 carries v1's execution counts but this is a fresh kernel, so run them
2. `[V1.0]` — set `XOFF_V1`/`YOFF_V1` ≥ 10 µm from R8's (−15, −15), or `MOVED_MANUALLY_V1 = True`. Check the Latin square print and `mean V = +0.00000`
3. `[V1.1]` — write and image; prints a quick n/9 hit count
4. `[V1.2]` — the confusion matrix, replicate spread, and drift monitor

`[V1.2]` distinguishes the three outcomes explicitly: diagonal (verified), mostly-diagonal with one weak director (likely the LDART blind spot rather than physics — R4's 62° row read weak on LDART while VDART said it worked), or all nine on the same director, which is the R8 drift signature and means void rather than falsified.

# Section 6: the confusion matrix is perfectly diagonal — 9/9

| | →56° | →116° | →176° | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **cmd 56°** | **3** | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| **cmd 116°** | 0 | **3** | 0 | 3 |
| **cmd 176°** | 0 | 0 | **3** | 3 |

Every panel's dominant director is the one it was commanded to. Three replicates of each of the three directors, in one frame, in a Latin square — so **this cannot be drift**. The frame-wide population barely moved (56°: 0.292→0.265, 116°: 0.467→0.427, 176°: 0.241→0.307), yet nine panels sorted themselves into three groups by command.

**C23 is verified with replication.** Mean w@cmd by direction: 0.460 (56°), 0.566 (116°), 0.528 (176°) — consistent across all three, and no director is weak.

## Two numbers that need care

**The "1/9 hit" line in `[6.2]` is a floor artefact, not a failure.** Your two baseline frames were taken at **different setpoints** — `LDART_0000` at 0.35 V and `LDART_0001` at 0.40 V. `align_floor` therefore measured setpoint sensitivity, not noise, and returned **0.092** instead of the ~0.01–0.02 it should. Requiring 3× that (0.28) rejected eight genuine panels. This is exactly PITFALLS §1.4: LDART_0028 vs 0029 differed by >50° in peak direction from a setpoint change alone.

The before/after pair itself is fine — `LDART_0002` matches `LDART_0001` at 0.40 V — so the confusion matrix, which uses argmax rather than a floor threshold, is unaffected. It's the *floor* that's unusable, and with it the hit count and the retention test.

**Retention is not measurable from this data.** Eight of nine panels report "below floor" for the same reason. The one that cleared it read **+18 %** — an increase, not a decay. With n = 1 and an inflated floor I'd treat that as noise rather than evidence against C25's −10 %/13 min. Worth noting though: **peak direction moved 0° in all nine panels** between t+29 and t+39 min. The direction is holding even where the amplitude wobbles, which is the more useful half of the retention question.

## A real anomaly worth flagging

**`|A|` fell from 40.9 pm at 0.35 V to 29.4 pm at 0.40 V** — a *higher* setpoint giving 28 % *less* signal. That's backwards for PFM and suggests 0.40 V is pressing hard enough to start suppressing response. Consistency also dropped 0.87 → 0.86, and Λ read 280 nm on `LDART_0001` against 325 nm on the other three, i.e. that one frame is the odd one out. Given it's your `b2` reference, that's worth knowing.

## What I'd do next, cheaply

**One more LDART frame at 0.40 V, right now.** Paired with `LDART_0003` that gives a genuine setpoint-matched floor, which retroactively fixes both the hit count and the retention numbers for all nine panels — 4.3 min to recover the two measurements this session couldn't make.

Then, if you want the retention curve, a frame at ~t+2 h and one tomorrow. The longest interval in the campaign is still 13 minutes, and the flat peak directions here hint the state may be far more stable than C25 suggested.

I'll hold off updating `FINDINGS.md` until the clean floor is in — the 9/9 matrix stands on its own, but I'd rather record C23's replication with a valid floor beside it.

## assistant — 2026-08-20T16:01:44

**Section 7** is in the notebook — header, `[7.1]`, `[7.2]`, `[7.3]`. Same area, same probe, no stage move.

## The design

Section 6's commanded directions already form a Latin square, so the free choice is the **rotation Δ** applied to each panel. By three-fold symmetry Δ is the physically meaningful variable, not the absolute start or target. Assigning Δ as a Latin square **orthogonal** to the start square gives every (start, Δ) pair exactly once:

```
  56   0 -> 56  | 116 +60 ->176 | 176 -60 ->116
 116 -60 -> 56  | 176   0 ->176 |  56 +60 ->116
 176 +60 -> 56  |  56 -60 ->176 | 116   0 ->116
```

| Δ | panels |
|---|---|
| **0** | 56→56, 176→176, 116→116 |
| **+60°** | 116→176, 56→116, 176→56 |
| **−60°** | 176→116, 116→56, 56→176 |

**Three replicates of each Δ, one from each starting direction.** That's what tests the symmetry claim: is +60° the same operation from any start, and is −60° equivalent to +60°? All six allowed transitions plus three no-op controls, in one write.

Δ is balanced across rows and columns, so a spatial gradient can't mimic a Δ effect. **One residual confound I can't remove:** with the start square fixed, orthogonality forces the *target* to be constant per column (56° / 176° / 116°). Target is the least causal of the three, but `[7.3]` prints a per-column check so you can rule it out.

## Why Δ = 0 is the control that earns its place

Three panels get re-commanded to the direction they already hold. C27 says the lattice is a **contraction to a fixed point**, so a second identical write should change little. A large gain there instead would mean it's dose-cumulative — and would revise C27.

## Two things this session fixes for free

**A valid floor.** `LDART_0002` and `LDART_0003` are both at 0.40 V with nothing written between them — a genuine setpoint-matched noise floor. `[7.3]` re-scores Section 6 against it, which should convert that misleading 1/9 hit count into something honest. The 9/9 confusion matrix never depended on the floor.

**Verification that the starting states held.** `[7.1]` measures each panel's actual direction at t+39 min and compares it to what Section 6 commanded, *before* overwriting. If any drifted, it says so and `[7.3]` reports the transition from the measured state rather than the commanded one.

## To run

`[7.1]` → `[7.2]` → `[7.3]`. About 22 min at Λ = 325 nm (576 pulses), 28 min if Λ reads 280.

**Keep the setpoint at 0.40 V.** `[7.1]` doesn't move the stage and doesn't retune from scratch, so registration against Section 6 is exact — but a setpoint change would break the comparison the same way it broke Section 6's floor.

Check three things at `[7.1]`: the design assertions pass (they'll raise if Δ isn't orthogonal), all nine panels report `HOLDS`, and the honest floor comes out near 0.01–0.02 rather than 0.092.

# Section 7 results — after fixing a labelling bug of mine

**My `[7.1]` reported "0/9 hold". That was wrong. The truth is 8/9.**

`fit_triad` returns `(φ₀, φ₀+60, φ₀+120)` with φ₀ ∈ [0,60). Section 6 fitted φ₀ = 56.5 → (56, 116, 176); `[7.1]` re-fitted φ₀ = 1.5 → (2, 62, 122). **Same physical triad within 5°, but the index→angle mapping rotated by one member**, so every panel was scored against a starting angle ~60° off. The writes were fine — only the labels were wrong.

## What actually happened

**Section 6's writes held for 90 minutes: 8/9 panels.** Errors of 0°, 0°, 5°, 5°, 5°, 7°, 7°, 10° — one failure (R0C1, 65° off). The previous longest retention interval in the whole campaign was 13 minutes.

**Section 7's rewrite: 8/9 reached target, p = 0.00097.**

| true Δ | reached | mean Δpower | panels |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0** (reinforce) | 3/3 | +0.162 | 116→122, 56→62, 176→2 |
| **+60°** | 2/3 | +0.160 | 176→62 ✓, 116→2 ✓, 56→122 ✗ |
| **−60°** | 3/3 | +0.155 | 56→2, 176→122, 116→62 |

Two things stand out. **+60° and −60° are indistinguishable** (+0.160 vs +0.155, difference +0.005 against a floor of 0.110) — the three-fold symmetry holds. And **Δ = 0 gains as much as the rotations** (+0.162): re-commanding a direction the panel already holds still raises order substantially. That's **cumulative, not saturated**, and it revises C27's contraction-to-a-fixed-point reading.

The magnitudes mostly sit under 3× the 0.110 floor, so the robust readout is the transition matrix, not the deltas. 8/9 by chance is p ≈ 0.001.

# Section 8 is in the notebook

**No, you don't need to change anything by hand.** `[8.1]` sets scan size and both offsets through `setup_scan(size_um=10.0, xoff_um=12.0, yoff_um=0.0)`. Leave the Igor panel alone.

**On the move distance:** 10 µm is the *minimum*. The old frame is 8 µm at offset (0,0), so it spans ±4 µm; a 10 µm frame needs its centre ≥ **(8+10)/2 = 9 µm** away. I defaulted to **12 µm** for 3 µm of clearance — 10 µm leaves only 1. `[8.1]` asserts the arithmetic and then checks height correlation against `LDART_0004` as independent evidence.

**On pixel size:** 10 µm at 256 px is 39 nm/px, which drops Nyquist to 12.8 µm⁻¹ — just under the 14 µm⁻¹ top of the q window, so its finest end aliases. # Theory

## T1 — the lattice pins walls; it does not rotate interiors

The ± pattern of period Λ creates a periodic in-plane field whose **sign boundaries are favourable wall positions**. Writing nucleates walls there and pins them. The order parameter is the *fraction of walls pinned*, not a degree of rotation.

| observation | explained by T1 |
|---|---|
| spacing must give sign period = Λ (C23) | template must match natural wall spacing |
| one pass ceilings near 0.35 | finite pinning probability per wall |
| a second identical write still gains +0.162 (§7, Δ=0) | each pass pins more of the unpinned walls |
| raster ∥ a family depletes it (C26) | tip travels **along** those walls, sweeping them out |
| rewriting costs nothing extra (C24) | walls equally mobile from any configuration |
| non-triad commands never take (R5) | walls only lie along allowed directions |
| pre-poling hurts (C27) | the raster already annihilated the walls the lattice needs |

T1 replaces the "contraction to a fixed point" reading, which described the ceiling but predicted nothing about §7's cumulative gain and had no mechanism for C26's directionality.

**Its sharpest prediction: intervention is only needed at walls.** Interiors need no pulses. Cost should scale with wall length, not area — which is your question 2.

# Hypotheses

**H1 — the lower size limit is set by the halo, not Λ.** A template needs one sign period (Λ ≈ 325 nm), but r_eff = 625 nm means one pulse already spans **1.25 µm**. Prediction: collapse below ~1.25 µm, *not* below 0.33 µm.

**H2 — no intrinsic upper limit to ~5 µm.** Under T1 a bigger region is only slower. Flat order parameter from 1.5 to 5 µm; if it falls, T1 needs an area-energy term.

**H3 — wall-only pulses match a full lattice with ~3× fewer points** (wall fraction ≈ ξ/Λ ≈ 0.29).

**H4 — masking already-aligned regions costs nothing.**

**H5 — perimeter-only writing aligns the interior**, with a measurable penetration depth. If so, large-area control scales as perimeter.

# Section 9 — the size ladder (answers Q1)

Four squares at **0.2, 1.0, 2.2, 4.0 µm physical size**, one commanded direction, plus a **21 µm² untouched control**, in one 10 µm frame. Spacing stays Λ/2 so dose per unit area is identical at every size — only the number of sign periods changes. Sizes are physical rather than in sign periods, so the ladder means the same thing at any Λ; pulse counts adapt (376–1108).

Two deliberate choices: the commanded director is the one **furthest from the virgin peak**, so success is a real rotation rather than reinforcement; and the largest square is written **first** as the positive control, so a failure costs ~14 min instead of 30. I'm re-raising staging because Section 8 shows the failure mode is a bad reference frame, not dose — your 10 V argument still holds for dose.

`[9.4]` locates L_min by bracketing and tests it against 1.25 µm, and compares the two largest sizes for H2.

## Also added to `[TOOLKIT]`

- **`frame_gate()`** — refuses a reference frame with r₁₂ < 0.40, low consistency, or |S| far below the session median. This is the guard Section 8 lacked, and `[9.1]` calls it on **both** baseline frames before anything is built.
- **`wall_mask()`, `mismatch_mask()`, `mask_to_sites()`** — ready for Section 10's adaptive patterns (H3–H5). `mask_to_sites` reports points kept vs total so the saving is quantified, and it drops the minority-sign excess rather than leaving net DC.

**To run:** `[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[9.1]` → `[9.2]` → `[9.3]` → `[9.4]`. Set `XOFF_S9`/`YOFF_S9` if you want the cell to move, or leave `MOVED_MANUALLY_S9 = True` since you're changing probe and area by hand. **Keep the setpoint fixed** across both baseline frames.

## assistant — 2026-08-20T20:32:02

Both objections are now design constraints rather than annoyances. **Section 10** replaces the size ladder.

## First, why `[9.1]` failed — my bug, not the sample

```
find_resonance swept -> 653.5 kHz
the DART loop actually tracked -> 627.0 kHz     offset 19.8 kHz
```

`find_resonance` took the **global argmax of the tune curve**, which was a different mode from the one the loop follows. With neither sideband on the peak, |A| fell to 20.6 pm and the gate rejected the frame. The gate was right; the tuning was wrong.

`tune_and_verify()` now checks the tune against a **64-line probe frame (~30 s)** and re-centres on the *tracked* frequency until the drive is within 12 kHz. It replaces `find_resonance` in `[9.1]` and is used in Section 10.

## Your complaint 1 — probe wear

Section 9 needed **376–1108 pulses, 22–37 min** of continuous 10 V contact. Section 10 needs **~64 + ~18 = 82 pulses, ~2.5 min.** That's not a compromise, it's the theory being tested: T1 says pulses in domain interiors do nothing.

## Your complaint 2 — a lost frame

Three changes:

- `tracking_rows()` reports which scan lines tracked and the **largest usable y-band**, so a partial frame gets scored instead of discarded. Calibrated on your data — the natural row-median MAD is 1.4–5.6 kHz, so my first ±1 kHz cut flagged everything; the working criterion is **max(10 kHz, 4×MAD)**, which gives 100 % on healthy frames and catches `LDART_0005` at 86 % with a usable band of 1.41–10.0 µm.
- `frame_gate()` now includes tracking. Worth noting the two Section 9 baselines failed for **different** reasons: `LDART_0010` on |S| (0.42 of median), `LDART_0009` on its 5.6 kHz MAD. Only one was being checked.
- **Both panels sit at the same y**, side by side, so a lost band takes both or neither and can never break the A-vs-B comparison asymmetrically. `[10.2]` checks explicitly whether both cores fall inside the tracked band.

## What Section 10 tests — H3

| panel | pattern | pulses |
|---|---|---|
| A | full lattice at the commanded director | 36–100 |
| B | same lattice, **only where `wall_mask` fires** | ~⅓ of A |

Measured on your real frame, `wall_mask` flags **33 %** of the area at the default `coh_max = 0.25` — matching ξ/Λ ≈ 0.29 closely, which is itself a small independent check on T1. The knob is calibrated: 0.15 → 13 % (7.9× saving), 0.25 → 33 % (3.1×), 0.35 → 57 % (1.8×).

The readout is Δpower at the command **and Δpower per pulse**. If B matches A, adaptive writing is established and every later experiment gets cheaper and gentler.

Geometry verified at every Λ and angle: halo gap +150 nm, two 6.4 µm² untouched control bands.

## And Q1 comes partly free

The panels are **1.4 µm** — essentially at H1's predicted floor of 2 r_eff = 1.25 µm. If both align, the small end of your first question is answered without the ladder. The **large** end is exactly the probe-damaging case, so it stays deferred until H5 (perimeter-only) can make it cheap — writing a boundary instead of an area is the only route to large regions that doesn't punish the tip.

**To run:** `[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[10.1]` → `[10.2]`. About 17 min. Section 9's cells remain if you ever want the full ladder, now with the tuning fixed.

## assistant — 2026-08-20T20:55:32

Fixed. Both frames now pass, and `strict=True` wouldn't stop them either.

## What was actually wrong with the check

With `ref_tags = (the other baseline,)`, the "session median" was a **single frame** — so `rel` was just the ratio of the two, and whichever was smaller got rejected however healthy it was. `LDART_0009` scored 2.39 and `LDART_0010` scored 0.42: **reciprocals of the same 2.4× difference**, seen from either end. Neither number said anything about absolute quality.

And you're right about the deeper point: **|S| has no absolute scale.** It moves with the probe, the setpoint and the tune, so a probe change legitimately shifts it and there's nothing to compare against.

Now:

- the |S|-relative test **only reports**, and only when ≥3 reference frames make a median meaningful
- with exactly two frames it reports the *pair inconsistency* instead — "these differ by 2.4×, check which is off before trusting a floor built from them", which is the genuinely useful part the old test was accidentally detecting
- the gate **warns by default** and raises only with `strict=True`, so the decision stays with you
- only `r12` and consistency can fail at all, since those are absolute — `r12 < 0` means the DART channels disagree and the signed map is corrupt regardless of probe

`LDART_0010` now reads: `r12 +0.85, consistency 0.80, tracked 100%` → **warnings only, usable**. And the triad pins cleanly from it: φ₀ = 0.0 → {0, 60, 120}, **2° from the film triad**, modulation 0.202 — normal virgin material. So that frame was fine all along.

## One thing I'd keep

The **19.8 kHz drive-versus-tracked offset** is a separate matter. A new probe fully explains why the resonance *moved* from 653 to 627 — that's expected for a new cantilever. It doesn't explain why the drive was left 20 kHz away from it, and that gap is why |A| read 20.6 pm instead of ~30–45.

But `tune_and_verify()` handles it by **self-correcting rather than blocking**: it re-centres on whatever frequency the loop actually tracks and retunes, so a new probe's resonance is found automatically wherever it lands. Nothing to relax there — it's the mechanism that makes the probe change a non-event.

Sections 9 and 10 both call the gate non-strict now. `[10.1]` is ready to run as-is.

## Section 10's panel A already answers the size question

Panel A is a **full lattice at 1.4 µm**, which is the same recipe and essentially the same size as Sections 6/7's 1.2–1.6 µm cores — and those gave 9/9 and 8/9. So A is a direct positive control at the size H1 predicts as the floor (2 r_eff = 1.25 µm). If A aligns, you know **L_min ≤ 1.4 µm** for free.

That also covers the one real risk of this ordering. If the 1.4 µm panels were below L_min, Section 10 would return a null for a *size* reason and I might misread it as a *masking* reason — but `[10.2]` checks A first and says so explicitly: *"A did not take, so H3 cannot be judged."* The failure modes stay separable.

## Running 9 first is exactly the cost you objected to

| | pulses | writing time |
|---|---|---|
| Section 9 | 376–1108 | 22–37 min |
| Section 10 | ~82 | ~2.5 min |

Section 9's 4 µm square alone is 576 of its ~760 pulses. Running it before knowing whether the cheap pattern works spends the probe on the expensive question first.

## If H3 holds, Section 9 gets ~3× cheaper

A wall-masked ladder would be ~250 pulses instead of ~760 — 8–12 min instead of 22–37. So Section 10 isn't a detour around Section 9; it's what makes Section 9 affordable.

## And Section 9's large end should wait for H5 regardless

The 4 µm square is the probe-damaging case, and **perimeter-only writing (H5) is the only route to large regions that doesn't punish the tip** — cost scaling as perimeter rather than area. H5 is downstream of H3.

## What you give up

Only the *bracket*. Section 10 tells you 1.4 µm works; it won't tell you where it stops working. That needs the small end of the ladder (0.2 and 1.0 µm), which is cheap — 4 + 36 pulses. Worth adding as a two-square mini-ladder alongside a masked run once H3 reports, rather than now.

## One navigation note

Section 9's cells sit at **57–60**, physically *above* Section 10 at **62–63**, so running top-to-bottom would hit `[9.1]` first. Go directly to `[10.1]`.

# Section 10: adaptive writing works, at reduced amplitude

Both panels **landed on the commanded direction to 1°**, and the wall-masked panel used **half the pulses**.

| panel | pattern | pulses | Δpower | peak err | per pulse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | full lattice | 100 | **+0.220** | 1° | 2.20 |
| **B** | wall-masked | **50** | **+0.149** | 1° | **2.99** |
| below | untouched | 0 | −0.037 | 89° | — |
| above | untouched | 0 | −0.036 | 89° | — |

Both controls moved the *other* way (−0.037, −0.036, peak stuck at 91°), so the effect is real and local. Floor 0.054.

**B/A order parameter 0.68; B/A per-pulse efficiency 1.36×.** The masked pattern is *more* efficient per pulse but reaches a lower total. So H3 is **partially supported**: pulses in domain interiors are not doing nothing, but they are worth less than pulses on walls.

The population vectors show the same thing — A drove w(0°) from 0.324 to **0.651**, B from 0.439 to 0.545. Both moved the right way; A moved further.

## Where T1 needs amending

T1 predicted B ≈ A. It got 0.68. So wall pinning is the *dominant* term but not the only one — there's a bulk contribution of roughly a third. The honest revision: **order parameter gain ≈ (wall term) + (smaller bulk term)**, with the wall term ~1.4× more efficient per pulse.

## Two caveats I'd flag before believing the 0.68

**The mask was looser than intended.** It flagged **43 %** of pixels against the ξ/Λ prediction of 31 %, so B kept 50 of 100 sites rather than the ~29 expected. That means B was *not* a clean "walls only" pattern — it was a half-density pattern that happened to favour walls. Some of the 0.68 could simply be dose. Distinguishing needs `coh_max = 0.15` (13 % of area, ~7.9× saving) as a third panel.

**Baseline b has r₁₂ = −0.71.** The channels anticorrelated on the very frame used as the "before" reference and to build the wall mask. `signed()` corrects the flip so the map is usable — and the relaxed gate correctly passed it — but it's the same frame type that caused trouble in Section 8, and the wall mask was computed from it. That may be exactly why the mask came out at 43 %.

Also worth noting: **Λ read 301 nm and modulation only 0.145** here, the lowest of any area (virgin range 0.17–0.25). Less texture to work with, which makes A's +0.220 the more impressive number.

## What I'd do next

**A three-panel dose-versus-mask discrimination**, ~15 min: full lattice (100 pulses) / tight mask at `coh_max = 0.15` (~13 pulses) / random half-density (50 pulses, mask-free). The random-half panel is the control that Section 10 lacked — if it matches B's 0.68, the saving was dose and the mask did nothing; if it comes in well below, the mask is real.

That's the cleanest way to convert "half the pulses got 68 %" into a proper efficiency curve, and it stays inside your constraints: ~163 pulses total, one 6 µm frame, ~20 min.

Your two operational objections are also now resolved in practice: **150 pulses versus Section 9's 376–1108**, and `tune_and_verify` fixed the tune on the first probe frame with no repeat of the 26 kHz error. Tracking held at 89–100 % across all four frames, and the after-frame's usable band covered both panel cores.

| **MASKED** | the N_keep sites with **lowest orientation coherence** (most wall-like) | 40 % of N |
| **RANDOM** | a **random** N_keep from the same lattice | same as MASKED |

Three 1.4 µm panels need 8 µm to keep their cores clear; the write is still only **~180 pulses, ~3 min**, against Section 9's 376–1108. Probe wear comes from the write, not the frame.

## assistant — 2026-08-20T22:37:15

# Section 11: the mask is real — it was not dose

**MASKED − RANDOM = +0.265, which is 4.6× the floor.** Identical pulse counts, so this is targeting, not dose.

| panel | pulses | Δpower | peak err | per pulse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FULL** | 100 | **+0.375** | 4° | 3.75 |
| **MASKED** | 40 | **+0.162** | 29° | **4.04** |
| **RANDOM** | 40 | **−0.103** | 61° | −2.58 |
| below | 0 | +0.049 | 54° | — |
| above | 0 | +0.054 | 29° | — |

Random 40 pulses didn't just underperform — it went **backwards**, −0.103, driving w(0°) from 0.319 to **0.534** while the command was 120°. So an untargeted subset actively pushed the texture the wrong way, and only the wall-ranked subset moved it toward the command.

The selection had real contrast: mean coherence **0.185** at masked sites vs **0.269** at random ones, a 1.45× separation, exactly as the dry run predicted.

## What this does to T1

T1 said pulses act at walls. That's now supported in the strongest available form — same dose, different sites, opposite outcomes. But the quantitative claim needs revising:

| | |
|---|---|
| MASKED/FULL | **0.43** at 40 % of the pulses |
| per-pulse efficiency | MASKED 4.04 vs FULL 3.75, only **1.08×** |

So wall sites are *necessary* but barely more efficient per pulse than the full lattice. That's not the ×3 saving T1 predicted. The honest reading: **the full lattice is already dominated by its wall-adjacent pulses** — at Λ/2 spacing with a 625 nm halo, nearly every pulse influences a wall, so removing 60 % of them removes roughly 57 % of the effect. The mask tells you *which* pulses matter; it doesn't buy you a free lunch.

Section 10's 1.36× per-pulse advantage now looks like noise from its loose 43 % mask and its r₁₂ = −0.71 reference frame.

## Two caveats

**Clean at every Λ and every commanded angle** now. **Section 12** is in the notebook.

## The design: an L, not a grid

Two axes crossing at one shared panel, so seven panels cover eight conditions:

| axis | panels | answers |
|---|---|---|
| **size** at full areal dose | 0.25, 0.5, **1.0**, 1.75 × 1.4 µm | H1 lower limit, H2 upper limit — the R9 questions |
| **dose** at the 1.0 size | **100 %**, 70 %, 40 %, 20 % wall-ranked | the efficiency curve |

The **1.4 µm full-lattice panel is shared** as both the size midpoint and the 100 % dose point. Spacing stays Λ/2 everywhere, so the size axis holds **areal dose constant** — only the number of sign periods inside the region changes. That's what makes it a size experiment rather than a dose experiment in disguise.

## Cost, and what that cost buys

| Λ | pulses | writing |
|---|---|---|
| 245 nm | 538–782 | 9–13 min |
| 301–325 nm | 310–606 | 5–10 min |
| 388 nm | 204–362 | 3–6 min |

**~27 min total.** Section 9 wanted 376–1108 pulses for the size axis *alone*.

The saving comes from capping the largest panel at 1.75 × 1.4 ≈ 2.4 µm, and I've stated the cost of that in the doc rather than burying it: **H2 is tested over a 1.75× size range, 3.1× in area, versus Section 9's 20×.** If order parameter is flat across it, the upper limit is *not* established — only that no fall appears within a factor of three in area. `[12.2]` says exactly that in its verdict rather than overclaiming.

## What `[12.2]` reports

- **H1**: brackets L_min between the largest failing and smallest succeeding size, and tests whether the bracket contains **2 r_eff = 1.25 µm**. The 0.35 and 0.7 µm panels sit below it, 1.4 and 2.4 above.
- **H2**: the two largest sizes compared against the floor.
- **Dose curve**: linear fit plus a low-half/high-half slope ratio. If the high half is under half the low half → **saturating**, there's an operating point at the knee and large areas become affordable. If the ratio is near 1 → **linear**, the mask is diagnostic only, cost scales with area, and H5 (perimeter-only) becomes the only route to large regions.

## Two fixes folded in

The dose row's x positions are now **derived from the measured extent** rather than a fixed 2.7 µm pitch — at Λ = 245–325 nm the 1.4 µm panel comes out 1.46–1.55 µm wide and the hard-coded pitch made neighbouring halos overlap in 6 of 12 configurations.

And since the tune drifted **24 → 37 → 14 kHz** across Section 11, `[12.1]` prints the drive-tracked offset for both baseline frames so drift is visible before you commit to the write.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
- PZTO(111) superdomains: six tetragonal polar variants, two C₃ᵥ orbits, three mechanical skeletons at 120° about [111], projecting to three stripe directors 60° apart — the **triad**
- **Film triad is a constant**: rigid one-parameter fit gives φ₀ within ~5° across 6+ areas; `FAM_FILM = (2.0, 62.0, 122.0)`
- **Population vector** w over the three directors + Λ (lamellar period, 245–400 nm) as the state variable
- **Rigid triad fit** (`fit_triad`): one free rotation φ₀ ∈ [0,60), members forced 60° apart; modulation depth separates virgin (~0.17–0.25) from poled (~0.53)
- φ₀ is **mod 60**, so re-fitting can rotate the index→angle mapping — the cause of a major labelling bug
- **DART modes**: LDART = lateral deflection lock-in, resonance 650 ± 200 kHz; VDART = vertical, 350 ± 200 kHz
- `tune_probe(readonly=True)` **does not sweep** — it returns the last stored tune curve and ignores center/width
- The swept argmax is **not** necessarily the mode the DART loop tracks (653.5 vs 627 kHz on 20 Aug)
- **r_eff = 625 nm** pulse halo; 2·r_eff = 1.25 µm sets a candidate minimum writable size
- Charge per pulse = |V| × dwell; dwell = PULSE_N × step / speed; PULSE_N=25 at 0.02 µm / 0.5 µm·s⁻¹ = **1.0 s = 10 V·s**
- C23 recipe: lattice at Λ/2 spacing so **sign period = Λ**, 10 V × 1 s, charge-balanced per panel
- **Latin square** and **Graeco-Latin (orthogonal) square** designs to decouple commanded direction / Δ / position from spatial drift
- **Theory T1 (wall-pinning template model)**: the lattice pins domain walls rather than rotating interiors; order parameter = fraction of walls pinned

## assistant — 2026-08-21T01:26:44

Analysis complete. Here's what R12 says.

## The write itself was clean

866 pulses, exactly charge-balanced (433 +, 433 −, mean V = 0.00000), all seven panels landed where intended, and the offset change to (0, +15) put the frame clear of all five earlier areas. The control band came back **Δ = +0.001 ± 0.014** across six tiles — genuinely untouched, which is what makes the rest of this trustworthy.

I took the geometry from the trajectory file rather than re-deriving it: re-fitting Λ on the reference frame now gives 231 nm against the ~234 nm used at write time, and that 1.3 % shift flips three of the four `n_side` roundings. Actual panels: **0.35 / 0.58 / 1.29 / 2.46 µm** and dose 100/70/40/20 % at 1.29 µm.

## Size axis — no upper limit, and cost scales with area

All measured in the same 1.29 µm window, so the instrument is constant:

| written | pulses | before | after | **Δ** | peak err | Δ×1000/pulse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.29 µm | 144 | 0.157 | 0.422 | **+0.265** | 1° | 1.84 |
| 2.46 µm | 484 | 0.253 | 0.578 | **+0.325** | 1° | 0.67 |

Floor 0.054, so these are 4.9× and 6.0×. Both lock to the commanded direction to **1°**. w(0°) goes 0.465 → 0.814 in the big panel.

**H2 holds:** order parameter is flat-to-slightly-rising across 1.9× in length, 3.6× in area. But pulses rose 3.4× for the same result — **per-pulse efficiency falls as 1/area**. Writing bigger works; it just costs proportionally more, so there's no economy of scale to find.

## Dose axis — this is the important result

| keep | pulses | **Δ** | peak err |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 % | 144 | **+0.265** | 1° |
| 70 % | 100 | +0.082 | 1° |
| 40 % | 58 | +0.033 | 1° |
| 20 % | 28 | **−0.076** | 89° |

**Only the full lattice clears the floor.** Linear fit slope 2.75e−3/pulse with intercept −0.151 → x-intercept at **55 pulses = 38 % of the lattice**. Slope ratio high-half/low-half = **+1.15: linear, not saturating.**

So the answer to the question Section 11 raised is the unwelcome one — **there is no knee to exploit.** You cannot buy most of the effect with a fraction of the pulses. And at 20 % the texture goes *backwards*, peak swinging to 91°, which is the second time sparse pulsing has actively disordered (Section 11's random panel did the same).

The real-space difference map explains why:

| panel | pulses | RMS change | vs matched control |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.35 µm | 16 | 1.409 | z = **+9.9** |
| 0.58 µm | 36 | 1.860 | z = **+33.8** |
| 1.29 µm | 144 | 1.553 | z = +36.7 |
| 2.46 µm | 484 | 1.598 | z = +56.8 |
| dose 70 % | 100 | 0.715 | z ≈ +3.7 |
| dose 40 % | 58 | 0.700 | z ≈ +3.2 |
| dose 20 % | 28 | 0.666 | z ≈ +2.0 |

Thinned lattices **barely perturb the material at all** — they didn't fail to *orient*, they failed to *act*. Meanwhile the 0.35 µm panel, with 16 pulses, changed the texture as strongly as the 2.46 µm panel with 484.

## Theory refinement: it's the periodicity, not the charge

T1 (wall-pinning template) predicted effect ∝ number of walls pinned, so roughly linear in pulse count with ~3× gain from ranking. Measured: 1.08× in Section 11, and now near-total collapse at 70 %. T1 is wrong in its simple form.

**T2 — coherent structure-factor model.** The lattice imposes a spatially *periodic* field at wavevector q = 2π/Λ, and the lamellae respond by commensuration. What matters is the structure factor at that q, not total charge. Removing a fraction of sites cuts the coherent amplitude, so Δ ∝ (fraction kept)², minus an incoherent disordering term:

| keep | (kept)²·0.265 − 0.06 | observed |
|---|---|---|

Rough at 40 %, but it gets the collapse and the sign reversal right — neither of which T1 predicts at all. T2 also explains the size-independence (structure factor is per unit area), the 1/area cost, and *why* Section 11's wall-ranked mask beat random at all: **walls are themselves periodic with period Λ**, so ranking by wall proximity selects a sub-lattice and preserves coherence better than random removal does.

T2 makes an uncomfortable prediction worth stating: **H5 (perimeter-only writing) should fail**, because a perimeter has no periodic interior field.

The discriminating test is cheap: compare **periodic decimation** against **random decimation at identical pulse count**, with sign period held at Λ in every arm so only the density varies. ## Two bugs, one of which reaches back

**1. The order parameter is undefined below ~0.94 µm.** `dir_power` needs ≥24 px *and* ≥4 stripe periods; at Λ = 234 nm both bind at 0.94 µm. My two sub-micron panels (1.5 and 2.5 periods) sit below it, so **H1 is not answered** — and this is a design error on my part: I sized the ladder in units of r_eff without checking the readout could resolve it. The limit is fundamental, not a pixel-count problem — you cannot measure a stripe direction in a box holding two stripes. Testing below 2 r_eff needs a different observable, and the difference-map result above suggests one that works.

**2. `dir_power` crops to `min(shape)`, so every wide control band I've passed it measured only a square at the band's left end** — for R12's band, 13 % of it. ## What today established

**The lattice sets the in-plane direction, reproducibly and rewritably.**
- Section 6: **9/9** diagonal confusion matrix — three commanded directions × three replicates, Latin square. Held **90 minutes** (8/9).
- Section 7: **8/9** transitions (p = 0.00097), with Δ = 0/+60/−60 all landing at +0.155 to +0.162. Three-fold symmetry is exact, and the "stay" panels gained as much as the rotations — the lattice is **cumulative, not saturated**.
- The film triad is a constant again: today's area fit 0/60/120, **2° from** `FAM_FILM` = 2/62/122. That's 7+ areas now.

**Size: works from 0.35 µm to 2.46 µm, with no economy of scale.**
- Δ flat-to-rising across 3.6× in area (+0.265 → +0.325), both locking to 1° of command.
- Per-pulse efficiency falls as **1/area**. Big regions work; they just cost proportionally more.
- 16 pulses at 0.35 µm perturbed the texture as strongly as 484 at 2.46 µm.

**Dose: the lattice is all-or-nothing.** Only 100 % clears the floor (+0.265). At 70 % → +0.082, 40 % → +0.033, 20 % → **−0.076 with the peak swinging to 91°**. Linear with a positive x-intercept at **38 % of the lattice**: no knee, no saturation. Thinned lattices barely touch the material (z ≈ 2–4 vs 37–57 for full ones).

## What it does to the theory

**T1 (wall-pinning template) is dead in its simple form.** It predicted effect ∝ walls pinned — linear in dose, ~3× gain from wall-ranking. Measured: 1.08× ranking gain, and near-total collapse at 70 % dose.

**T2 (coherent structure factor) replaces it.** The lattice acts through the *periodicity* of the imposed field at q = 2π/Λ, not through total injected charge. Δ ∝ (fraction kept)² minus an incoherent disordering term — which reproduces both the collapse and the sign reversal. It also retroactively explains why wall-ranking beat random at all: **walls are periodic with period Λ**, so ranking selects a sub-lattice and preserves coherence.

Three consequences:
1. **Adaptive/sparse patterns are a dead end** for reducing cost — the answer to question 2 is essentially "no, not by thinning."
2. **H5 (perimeter-only writing) should fail** — a perimeter carries no periodic interior field. T2 predicts against the one route I'd been holding out for large areas.
3. The route to affordability, if one exists, is **changing q rather than removing sites**.

## Next

1. **The discriminating experiment**: periodic decimation vs random decimation at *identical* pulse count, sign period pinned at Λ in every arm. T2 says periodic-half performs like the full lattice; T1 says they're indistinguishable. ~4 panels, ~350 pulses, one 8 µm frame. This is the cheapest high-information test we have.
2. **Re-derive Section 11 before it enters `FINDINGS.md`.** Its control band sat inside the written strips, and the panels were 119 vs 61 pulses, not equal.
3. **Question 1's lower limit needs a new observable.** The order parameter is undefined below ~4Λ ≈ 0.94 µm — you can't measure a stripe direction in a box holding two stripes. The difference-map statistic that worked today (z = +9.9 at 0.35 µm) is the candidate.

Two caveats on today's numbers: `[12.1]` picked the reference frame by r12 alone and chose the one tracking only 67 % of lines, blind below y = 3.3 µm — so the dose row's wall ranking came from untracked rows (r = 0.72 against the good frame, degraded but not random). And the `dir_power` crop bug means any wide control band I've scored measured only a square at its left end.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T01:56:46

Built and dry-run clean. **Section 13** is at cells **70–72**.

## The design

The full lattice sits at spacing Λ/2 with the sign alternating by row, so the template has **period Λ along the row normal, running along the commanded direction** — commensurate with the lamellae it's trying to create. Charge is held identical across three thinned arms and only the *geometry* of the removal changes:

| arm | thinned by | sign period | pulses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FULL** | — | Λ | n² |
| **P50** | every other **column** — along the stripes | **Λ, intact** | n²/2 |
| **W50** | row pairs (0,1),(4,5)… — across the stripes | **2Λ, wrong** | n²/2 |
| **R50** | random half, ± matched | aperiodic | n²/2 |

The key asymmetry: thinning *along* the stripes cannot change the sign period, while thinning *across* them necessarily does, because the sign period is always twice the row spacing. So P50 and W50 differ in exactly the quantity T2 says is decisive while carrying identical charge.

**P50 vs R50 is the single decisive comparison** — same panel, same pulse count, same charge, differing only in whether the ± template stayed periodic. Predictions are written into `[13.1]` *before* the write: T1 says all three halves land at +0.13; T2 says +0.25 / ~0 / +0.07.

`[13.2]` scores the four arms in one matched window, computes the floor from 5–16 tiled control boxes in two bands, adds the real-space change statistic that separated "did nothing" from "did the wrong thing" in R12, and reports which model fits better by rms deviation — including an explicit "NOTHING WROTE" branch so a null can't be read as a result.

## Verified across the whole parameter space

I swept the real solver over 33 combinations of Λ (220–430 nm) and commanded angle:

- **all 33 fit**, charge balance exact everywhere, the three half-arms always at exactly n²/2
- **360–640 pulses → 6–11 min of writing** (Section 12 cost 866)
- Λ ≥ 355 nm needs more room, so the frame steps 10 → 12 µm automatically

## Four fixes folded in

Nothing about the geometry is hard-coded — the readout window derives from Λ and pixel size, the panel size from the window, the layout from the resulting halo. That closes the failure mode that has now cost three experiments (`[9.1]`'s dry-run `N_SIDE`, `[12.1]`'s dose-row pitch, and my own first draft of this cell, which used a 1.15 µm window holding **3.5 periods** at Λ = 325 nm).

Also fixed: `dir_power` now **warns before cropping** a non-square region; `tune_and_verify` takes and forwards the offsets (in Section 12 its probe frame landed on Section 11's written area); and `pick_ref` applies the r12 gate *before* coverage — the first dry run had it choosing a frame at **r12 = −0.81** over one at +0.93 because the bad frame had better line coverage.

## To run

`[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → **`[13.1]`** → **`[13.2]`** — cells **71–72**. About **30 min** total: ~15 min in `[13.1]` (tune, probe, scout frame, two baselines), ~15 min in `[13.2]` (write plus one frame).

Default offset **(12, 15)**, verified clear of all six areas used today *at the worst-case 12 µm frame* — the S8 and S12 clearances are the tight ones at 11.5 µm required against 12.0 available, so don't nudge it without re-running the guard.

In `[13.1]`, check the scout's Λ, the `margin ... per side` line, `layout OK`, and `mean V +0.000000` before letting `[13.2]` write. If any arm comes back within 2× the floor, re-run both cells with `ARM_ROT = 1` — that rotates the arm→position assignment and separates arm from position, which one replicate cannot.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T03:31:11

Decisive — and it refutes the model I built it to test.

## The result

Λ = 280 nm, commanded 4° against a virgin peak at 66° (62° away). n_side 16, so **FULL = 256 pulses and each half = 128**, charge exactly balanced.

| arm | pulses | sign period | before | after | **Δ** | peak err | vs floor | Δ×1000/pulse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FULL** | 256 | Λ | 0.094 | 0.436 | **+0.341** | 3° | 3.2× | 1.33 |
| **P50** | 128 | Λ (intact) | 0.104 | 0.111 | +0.007 | 60° | 0.1× | 0.05 |
| **W50** | 128 | 2Λ | 0.151 | 0.181 | +0.031 | 87° | 0.3× | 0.24 |
| **R50** | 128 | aperiodic | 0.182 | 0.193 | +0.011 | 87° | 0.1× | 0.09 |

Control: 7 tiles, Δ = −0.005 ± 0.049. Floor 0.108 (set by |b1−b2| on the edge tile), 3× = 0.324.

FULL is the **strongest alignment of the campaign** — w(4°) 0.214 → 0.595 while w(124°) collapses 0.474 → 0.082, peak locked to 1°. And **all three halves are dead**: 2–9 % of FULL, none clearing the floor.

**P50 / FULL = 0.02.** T2 predicted 0.95. T1 predicted 0.50.

## My prediction was wrong for a reason worth stating

T2's rms deviation (0.132) is worse than T1's (0.108), but neither model is vindicated — the halves are indistinguishable from *each other*, which is T1's qualitative claim, yet they sit at ~2 % rather than T1's 50 %.

The deeper problem is my own reasoning. I predicted P50 ≈ 0.95·FULL on the grounds that dropping columns leaves the sign period at Λ. But a structure-factor amplitude scales with the **number of contributing sources**, and P50 removes half of them — so a correctly formulated T2 predicts **0.5× for all three halves**, exactly like T1. My "decisive comparison" was not a discriminator between T1 and T2 at all. I conflated preserving the *period* with preserving the *amplitude*.

So the experiment did not settle the question I posed. It settled a better one.

## What it did establish

**The response is threshold-like, and the geometry of the thinning is irrelevant.** Three completely different 50 % geometries — thinned along the stripes, across them, and at random — all gave the same null. Put beside Section 12:

| density | Δ | fraction of full |
|---|---|---|
| 100 % (S13) | +0.341 | 1.00 |
| 100 % (S12) | +0.265 | 1.00 |
| 70 % (S12) | +0.082 | 0.31 |
| **50 % (S13, ×3 geometries)** | **+0.007 to +0.031** | **0.02–0.09** |
| 40 % (S12) | +0.033 | 0.12 |
| 20 % (S12) | −0.076 | < 0 |

The knee is between **70 % and 100 %** of full lattice density, and it is steep. Nothing about *which* sites you remove matters — only how many.

One clean subsidiary result: the real-space statistic shows **all four arms perturbed the film hard** — z = +43.6, +28.5, +18.6, +23.9 against control 0.507 ± 0.019. The halves failed to *orient*, not to *act*. That rules out the tip having stopped writing, and it distinguishes this null from Section 12's thinned panels, which barely touched the film at all (z = +2 to +4) despite carrying *more* charge per unit area. I don't have an explanation for that difference and won't invent one.

## Implications

**Question 2 is closed negatively.** Adaptive, masked, or sparse patterns cannot reduce the cost of writing in-plane order. You must pay full areal density at Λ/2 spacing, everywhere you want alignment. Section 11's wall-ranking advantage (1.08× per pulse) was never going to scale into anything useful, and now we know why: there is no sub-threshold regime to be clever in.

**H5 (perimeter-only) is almost certainly dead too** — a perimeter is an extreme thinning of the interior, and thinning by 2× already costs everything.

**The theory needs to be about a threshold, not a proportionality.** Both T1 and T2 are linear-response models and both fail. What survives is: a complete Λ/2 lattice orients; anything measurably less than complete does not.

## What I'd do next

**Locate the knee: a density ladder at 100 / 90 / 80 / 70 %** in one frame, single geometry (random is fine now that geometry is ruled out). Four panels, ~700 pulses, ~12 min of writing. If the effect only exists above ~90 %, that's a sharp physical number and a strong constraint on any mechanism.

**Then ask whether more is better:** Λ/4 spacing at 4× the pulses. If the response is threshold-like rather than saturating, over-driving may push Δ well past +0.341 — worth knowing before any attempt at a large area.

`FINDINGS.md` is now four sections behind (6–13) and Section 11 still needs re-deriving after the control-band bug. Say the word and I'll write all of it up in one pass.

## `FINDINGS.md` — 682 → 904 lines

**New conclusions C29–C35:**

| | | grade |
|---|---|---|
| **C29** | Lattice→direction replicates **9/9** in a Latin square; 8/9 held at +90 min | **A** |
| **C30** | All three Δ (0, ±60°) equally accessible; lattice writes are **cumulative** | **B** |
| **C31** | The film triad is one constant, `FAM_FILM` = 2/62/122, within ~5° over 8 areas | **A** |
| **C32** | Order parameter is size-independent 1.3–2.5 µm; per-pulse cost falls as **1/area** | **B** |
| **C33** | Below ~4Λ the order parameter doesn't exist — but writing still acts at 0.35 µm | **B** |
| **C34** | **The lattice is a threshold actuator in areal density, and thinning geometry is irrelevant** | **A** |
| **C35** | Wall-ranked masking beats random at equal dose | **W — withdrawn** |

**Revisions:** C1's specific angles superseded by C31; **C27 downgraded B → C** (Section 7 showed prior writing doesn't spend the resource — that was poling-specific, n = 1).

**§2 rewritten** — Q1/Q1b closed (the lattice does it, not the trajectory), Q2 subsumed by C34. New Q8 (where is ρc), Q9 (does over-driving help), Q10 (what mechanism gives a geometry-blind threshold), Q11–Q12. Q6 downgraded to "worse than unresolved": the real-space *orientation* metric disagreed with the FFT by 2–10× on virgin film and saturated at exactly 0.000/1.000 in small boxes, so it's unusable for populations — the real-space *difference* statistic is a different quantity and is sound.

**§3 gained 10 operational lessons**, including the `dir_power` crop that voided Section 11, the two independent window-size floors, and the two found while building today's code (below). **§4 rebuilt** around the working recipe and the readout constraints. **§5**: item 1 struck as achieved; item 2 now reads "closed negatively"; item 3 — *a mechanism* — is named as the main theoretical gap.

## Sections 14 and 15 — cells 73–78

**Section 14 (`[14.1]`, `[14.2]`, cells 74–75)** — the density knee. 100/90/80/70 % in one frame, random thinning (geometry is ruled out, so it isn't worth spending panels on), ± sets drawn separately so every panel is exactly charge-balanced. `[14.2]` pools the four new points with Section 12's and Section 13's, normalised to each session's own full-lattice value, and fits a power law against a step. **Predictions are printed before the write.** Note the honest tension already visible: Section 12's 70 % point (+0.082) sits on the ρ⁴ line, so if that reproduces, "threshold" in C34 should soften to "steeply super-linear" and the exponent becomes the number to quote.

**Section 15 (`[15.1]`, `[15.2]`, cells 77–78)** — over-drive. Λ/2 against Λ/4 with the sign alternating every **two** rows in the dense panel, holding the template period at Λ while quadrupling areal density; `[15.1]` refuses to run if the two panels' template periods differ, which would confound density with commensuration. One shared readout window sized to the smaller extent. `[15.2]` adds a VDART orbit check, because 4× density with r_eff = 625 nm is exactly where P7's non-monotonic window and C13's re-poling could bite.

**Verified over 30 Λ×angle combinations each: 0 failures, both sections.** S14 490–870 pulses, S15 544–832.

## Three bugs found while building

**The write time was 2× what I quoted.** `lattice_panel` selected sites by sign, returning all `+` then all `−`, so the tip crossed the panel between every pulse: 870 sites → 62,054 points → **41.4 min**. Serpentine ordering gives 30,459 points and **20.3 min**, with median step exactly one lattice spacing. Both build cells now print the travel overhead and warn above 2×. Writing time is pulses × 1.0 s × ~1.35, not pulses × 1.0 s — my earlier "~14.5 min" was wrong.

**Two toolkit name collisions.** `[11.1]` defines `lattice_sites` and `[8.2]` defines `build_lattice` — both names I'd reached for. Running those sections first would have silently rebound them with incompatible signatures. Now `lattice_panel`, audited against all 102 `def`s in the notebook: **47 toolkit exports, 0 shadowed**, plus an `inspect.signature` guard at the top of each build cell.

**A division by the normaliser.** `[14.2]` divides by the 100 % panel's Δ, gated only on 3× floor — which lets a near-zero through when the floor is itself small. Now gated on `max(3×floor, 0.02)`.

## Run order

`[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[14.1]` → `[14.2]`, then `[15.1]` → `[15.2]` as a separate run.

Section 14 defaults to offset **(26, 15)** — same y as Section 13, so minimal stage travel — and Section 15 to **(26, 28)**; both verified clear of all prior areas at the worst-case 12 µm frame. Run 14 first: ρc determines whether Λ/2 sits just above the knee or far above it, which changes what "over-driving" even means.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T13:03:27

All four cells clean. Here's what the two runs say.

## Section 15 — the strongest result of the campaign

Λ = 280 nm, commanded 124° against a virgin peak at 59°. Floor 0.098 from **14 control tiles in two bands** (Δ mean −0.009 ± 0.026).

| panel | spacing | pulses | **Δ** | peak err | vs floor | Δ×1000/pulse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REF** | Λ/2 | 144 | +0.159 | **0°** | 1.6× | 1.11 |
| **OVER** | Λ/4 | 400 | **+0.462** | 8° | **4.7×** | **1.16** |

The population tells it better than the Δ does:

```
OVER   w(4°)  0.307 -> 0.106
       w(64°) 0.329 -> 0.044
       w(124°) 0.364 -> 0.851      <- commanded
```

**w(commanded) = 0.851.** That's a near-single-variant state, and far past anything we've reached before.

Three things follow:

**Q9 answered: still climbing.** OVER − REF = +0.303 = 3.1× floor. Λ/2 is not the ceiling — it's near the *bottom* of the useful range.

**Per-pulse efficiency is identical: 1.11 vs 1.16.** 2.8× the pulses bought 2.9× the effect. So above threshold the response is **linear in pulse count with no diminishing return**, right up to w = 0.85. That is a different animal from what C34's "threshold" language suggests: dead below, then linear, no saturation.

**No re-poling.** VDART after the write: up 46/54 %, |⟨e^iφ⟩⟩| 0.390, two classes balanced, gate open. 4× areal charge did not flip the out-of-plane state, so P7's non-monotonic-window worry doesn't bite here.

One caveat I'd flag: w = 0.851 is close to the metric's ceiling of 1.0, so linearity **cannot** continue much further — a Λ/8 point would saturate by exhausting the population, not by any change in mechanism. The linear regime is established between Λ/2 and Λ/4 and no wider.

## Section 14 — void, and my fault

The control band drifted **−0.110 across every tile**, giving a floor of 0.199 — larger than the biggest panel signal.

The cause is in the hygiene table: **baseline b (LDART_0035) has |S| = 12.9 and r12 = 0.76**, against ~30–32 and 0.94–0.95 for the scout, baseline a, and the after-frame. Two of three usable frames agree; 0035 is the outlier. A weak |S| makes the FFT noise-dominated, and noise is isotropic, which inflates every directional bin — so 0035 read systematically *high* at 0° and everything looked like it fell.

**The design flaw is mine.** `[14.2]` took its triad and layout from `pick_ref`'s choice (0034) but computed every delta against `f14_b2` (0035). Those should be the same frame. Re-scoring against 0034:

| keep | pulses | Δ | peak err |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 % | 256 | +0.210 | 1° |
| 90 % | 230 | +0.051 | 1° |
| 80 % | 204 | +0.168 | 1° |
| 70 % | 180 | +0.132 | 1° |

Better, but still not an answer: the floor inherits |b1 − b2| = 0.156 from the bad-frame disagreement, and the sequence is **non-monotonic** — 90 % is the *lowest*. That's not a density curve. The starting values ranged 0.234 to 0.428, so Δ is confounded by where each panel began; the 90 % panel started highest and had least room.

**What Section 14 does support:** all four panels locked their peak to the commanded 0° within 1° and all four raised w(0°) — so **70 % density still writes**, which sits against a sharp threshold at 90 %. Combined with Section 13's 50 % failing to lock at all (err 60–87°), the transition is somewhere between 50 % and 70 %, which is where it already was. **Q8 is not answered.**

I've fixed both cells: the delta is now scored against `F_REF`, and **three baselines** are taken instead of two — with two there's no majority when they disagree, which is exactly how this answer was lost.

## What I'd do next

Re-run Section 14 as-is with the three-baseline fix — it's ~20 min and the question is still the right one. But Section 15 changes the priority: since per-pulse efficiency is constant above threshold and w = 0.851 is reachable, the interesting question is no longer only "how little can we get away with" but **"what does the Λ/4 recipe do to the things we thought were settled"** — the 90-minute retention (C29), the size independence (C32), and the sub-micron limit (C33), all of which were measured at Λ/2 near the bottom of the range.

Want me to update `FINDINGS.md` with C36 (over-drive) and the Section 14 void, and rebuild Section 16 around Λ/4 retention and size?

Section 14's two baselines disagreed about the starting director in **all four** panels: 0034 said 60°, 0035 said 0° — and 0° was the commanded direction, the worst possible coincidence. Measured on untouched film only:

| frame | role | \|S\| | streak index | control-band population (0/60/120) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0033 | scout | 28.6 | 0.060 | 0.462 / 0.278 / 0.260 |
| **0034** | baseline a | 30.5 | 0.069 | **0.407** / 0.326 / 0.267 |
| **0035** | baseline b | **12.9** | **0.115** | **0.569** / 0.242 / 0.189 |
| **0036** | after | 32.3 | 0.077 | **0.398** / 0.324 / 0.278 |

Scan lines run along x, so line-to-line offsets put FFT power on the q_y axis — which `dir_power` maps to a stripe director of **0°**. LDART_0035 has 1.5–1.9× the streak index of the other three and reads high at exactly 0°, with no domains involved. It's outvoted 3-to-1.

And 0034 → 0036 in the untouched band is **0.407 → 0.398 / 0.326 → 0.324 / 0.267 → 0.278** — an essentially perfect null. That's a clean before/after pair.

## Section 14 is not void — it's the best result we have

Every panel was an equivalent **60° rotation** (all four started dominant at 60°, all were commanded to 0°), same area, same frame pair:

| density | pulses | before | after | lead after | vs control floor | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 % | 256 | 60° | **0°** | +0.204 | 2.3× | rotated |
| 90 % | 230 | 60° | **0°** | +0.059 | 0.7× | rotated, weak |
| 80 % | 204 | 60° | **0°** | +0.590 | 6.8× | rotated |
| 70 % | 180 | 60° | **0°** | +0.158 | 1.8× | rotated |

**4/4.** Control: 0 of 6 tiles changed dominant director, Δlead −0.009 ± 0.058.

Set against Section 13, where all three 50 % arms were also 60° rotations from 64° → 4°:

| | before | after | lead | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL 100 % | 124° | **4°** | +0.307 | rotated |
| P50 50 % | 64° | 64° | −0.375 | **failed** |
| R50 50 % | 64° | **124°** | −0.075 | **failed — wrong director** |
| W50 50 % | ambiguous | 4° | +0.003 | tie, no result |

**The direction threshold is between 50 % and 70 % of the full Λ/2 lattice.** That answers Q8 — which I told you last turn was unanswered. It also means C34's "full lattice or nothing" is too strong: 70 % rotates the superdomains.

C34's other claim survives intact — thinning geometry is irrelevant. P50, W50 and R50 all failed on direction too.

## Section 15's headline is withdrawn

| panel | before dominant | commanded | task |
|---|---|---|---|
| REF Λ/2 | **64°** | 124° | a genuine 60° rotation |
| OVER Λ/4 | **124°** | 124° | **already on target — a sharpening** |

The two panels were not given the same task. OVER's w(commanded) = 0.851 is still the purest state we've produced, but it started at 0.437 while REF started at 0.178. Per-pulse gain in w(commanded): **REF 1.61, OVER 1.04 per 1000** — over-driving looks *worse*, though w is bounded by 1 and OVER is deep into saturation, so that comparison isn't clean either.

**Q9 is not answered.** My "still climbing, Λ/2 is not the ceiling" was an artifact of reading Δ magnitude on two panels with different starting states. What is established: Λ/4 reaches w = 0.851 without re-poling (VDART 46/54, gate open).

## The design flaw underneath this

The commanded director was chosen once per frame, as the triad member farthest from the **frame-wide** virgin peak. But local texture varies: OVER's position already favoured 124°. Section 14 got lucky — all four panels happened to start at 60°.

The fix is to choose the command **per panel, 60° from that panel's own local dominant director**, so every panel performs an equivalent rotation. That removes the largest confound in the campaign and would also shrink Section 14's panel-to-panel scatter (the 90 % panel is weakest largely because it started with the least room).

It also retroactively weakens Section 12's dose ladder as a density curve: its 70 % panel was a *hold* (already at 0°) while 40 % and 20 % were rotations, so those points aren't comparable to each other.

Two things I'd do: update `FINDINGS.md` — C34 revised to a 50–70 % bracket, a new conclusion that direction is the robust observable and Δpower is not, and Section 15 marked as confounded — and rebuild Section 16 around per-panel commanded directions, re-testing Λ/4 against Λ/2 with matched rotation tasks. Four panels, **two per spacing on the anti-diagonal** so neither condition is systematically earlier in the scan, rotation senses balanced ±60°. Both spacings hold the template period at Λ (Λ/4 alternates sign every *two* rows), and `[16.1]` refuses to run if they differ.

The core fix: `command_for()` reads each panel's **own local population** and commands the neighbouring triad member. Verified on real data — **0 of 32 position/sense combinations failed the 60° check**. And the retrospective test is the convincing one:


So Section 16 would have caught the exact confound that made C38 a C.

`[16.2]` reports direction first — dominant director before/after, the lead against a floor built from control tiles scored on *the same quantity*, and the untouched-tile director-flip rate as an explicit false-positive rate. Δ(angular power) appears last, labelled as continuity with Sections 12–15 and not the basis of any verdict.

It also reports **within-condition scatter** alongside the between-condition gap, and warns if the scatter exceeds 2× the floor — because if two panels with the same task and recipe disagree that much, every n = 1 comparison in Sections 12–15 needs re-reading.

## Two problems the dry run found and I fixed

**The `min_lead` guard raised after three baselines were already on disk** — 13 min of imaging for a refusal, because one panel landed where the dominant director led by only 0.027 and the baselines disagreed on it. `[16.1]` now searches a 3×3 grid of shifts for the whole block and picks the placement maximising the *worst* panel's lead, raising only if no placement works. Free, since it's all read off the reference frame.

**Per-panel commands mean per-panel extents.** The lattice extent scales as |cos| + |sin|, which varies **1.30×** across a triad, so sizing at one arbitrary member left some panels smaller than designed. Sizing now uses the triad member with the *smallest* factor and clearance the *largest*, with a per-panel extent-vs-window assertion once the commands are known.

Both deliverables are done; the final Section 16 dry run is still verifying. Summary:

## `FINDINGS.md` — 904 → 1054 lines

**C34 revised in place** to "needs **50–70 %** of full Λ/2 density", old text kept on a superseded line.

**Three new conclusions:**

| | | grade |
|---|---|---|
| **C36** | Score the **direction**, not Δ(angular power) — with the streak mechanism, the 3-to-1 majority test, and the numbers | **A** |
| **C37** | 70 % still rotates the superdomains; 50 % does not (**4/4 vs 0/3**, equivalent 60° rotations) | **B** |
| **C38** | Λ/4 reaches w = 0.851 without re-poling; whether it beats Λ/2 is **untested** | **C** |

Q8 struck as answered. Q9 reopened with the confound named. New **Q13** (how much scatter is unequal starting states) and **Q14** (does the 0° streak artefact contaminate C23/C29/C30, which also commanded near 0° — nothing earlier was screened). Seven operational lessons added.

## Section 16 — cells 79–81

**Two panels, run twice** (`RUN = 1`, then `RUN = 2` swaps the positions). `command_for()` reads each panel's own local population and commands the neighbouring triad member — verified on real data, **0 of 32 position/sense combinations** came out as anything but a 60° turn. And the retrospective test is the one that matters:

```
REF  L/2   local dominant  64 -> would have commanded 124
OVER L/4   local dominant 124 -> would have commanded   4
                              (Section 15 commanded 124 for both)
```

`[16.2]` reports direction first, with the untouched-tile director-flip rate as an explicit false-positive rate. Δ(angular power) appears last, labelled continuity-only.

## Three problems the dry runs found

**A geometry bug in `solve_grid`, affecting real data.** The written region is a square of side `L = (n−1)·spacing` **rotated** by the command; an axis-aligned window of side `W` fits only if `W·ANG ≤ L`. The code required `L ≥ W/ANG` — looser by `ANG²`, up to 1.93×. Not conservative, *insufficient*. Section 15 commanded 124° and needed L ≥ 1.63 µm but had **1.54** (REF) and **1.33 µm** (OVER), so the window corners overhung by 0.05 and 0.15 µm. Both are far inside r_eff = 625 nm, so **C38's numbers stand** — but one Section 16 panel failed the correct rule by 0.01 µm, so it's fixed now rather than after the next write.

**The 2×2 cost 1664 pulses — 35 min of continuous writing.** The commanded angle sets the cost (a Λ/4 panel is 576 pulses at 4° and 1024 at 64°), and the corrected rule inflated it further. Restructured to two runs of ~772 pulses, **≈16 min each**, which also means a mid-write tracking loss costs one replicate rather than the experiment.

**The `min_lead` guard raised after three baselines were on disk.** `[16.1]` now searches a 3×3 grid of placements for the whole pair and picks the one maximising the *worst* panel's lead, raising only if none works.

One correction to what I said last message: I quoted "~1000 pulses ≈ 22 min" for the 2×2. The real figure under the corrected geometry was 1664 pulses and 35 min — the estimate was wrong because it predated the window fix.

## To run

`[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[16.1]` → `[16.2]` with `RUN = 1`, offset **(0, 30)**; then set `RUN = 2` (offset auto-switches to **(14, 30)**) and repeat. ~33 min per run.

Before letting either write: check the three streak indices, the placement search's worst-case lead, that all three baselines agree on each panel's dominant director, and the `side` vs `W·ANG` line per panel.

`[16.1]` now runs end to end. The build output, all correct:

| | spacing | n | side | window needs | pulses | command |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REF** | 140 nm | 16 | 2.10 µm | 1.30 µm ✓ | 256 | 4° |
| **OVER** | 70 nm | 28 | 1.89 µm | 1.30 µm ✓ | 784 | 4° |

**Density ratio exactly 4.0×**, template period 280 nm = 1.0 Λ for both, travel overhead 1.24× with median step exactly one spacing, mean V +0.000000. Both panels' `side` clears the corrected `W·ANG` rule with room to spare — which the old rule would not have guaranteed.

The machinery all fired correctly:

- **10 µm didn't fit → escalated to 12 µm and re-took the baselines.** That path had never been exercised before.
- **Placement search** found a shift giving a worst-panel lead of **0.247**, five times the 0.05 minimum.
- **Cheap sense chosen explicitly**: both panels commanded to 4°, with the alternative cost printed (400 and 1024 pulses — so the choice saved 1.4× and 1.3×).
- **Streak screen** ran on all three baselines.
- The "baselines disagree" warning fired on the OVER panel — a stub artifact here, since my harness fed it a VDART frame as a baseline, but it confirms the warning path works.

Two things I've corrected as a result:

**`MAX_PULSES` raised 1000 → 1250.** The design comes to 1040 pulses = **21.5 min of writing**, 4 % over a cap I'd set arbitrarily. The cap exists to stop a fine Λ quietly becoming an hour of writing, not to block the intended design.

**One cost I should flag rather than bury:** the layout envelope is computed from the *worst-case* command (124°, ANG 1.388) because positions must be fixed before the commands are known. Both panels then came out at 4° (ANG 1.067), so their real halos are smaller than the envelope — and that conservatism is what forced the 12 µm frame. At 12 µm the window becomes pixel-limited (26 px = 1.22 µm rather than 4.2Λ = 1.18), which pushes OVER from 576 to 784 pulses. So the safety margin costs about 1.36× in pulses. Re-solving after the commands are chosen would be circular, so I've left it conservative — but that's why this run is 21.5 min rather than the 16 I quoted earlier.

`[16.2]` executed for the first time and the whole readout chain works — control tiles, lead floor, direction table, VDART check, populations, Δpower last.

It also exposed a logic flaw worth fixing, which I've just done.

## The flaw

In the dry run the control floor came out at **0.790** and the dominant director flipped in most untouched tiles — the stub's frames were simply incomparable. But the verdict printed:

> `-> NEITHER TURNED. Check the write gate before comparing.`

That points at the tip when the problem is the frames. **It's the same confusion that cost Section 14 a day** — a bad baseline read as a failed experiment.

`[16.2]` now computes an explicit `FLIP_RATE` — how often the dominant director changes on **untouched film**, which grades the readout and nothing else (Sections 12–15 ran 0/6 to 2/6) — and branches on it:

- **flip rate > 25 % or lead floor > 0.25** → *"UNREADABLE, not unsuccessful. The untouched control changed direction as much as the panels did… Retake the baselines; the written panels are still there and can be re-scored."*
- **readout sound, but nothing turned** → *"This is a real null: run `[WGATE]` before writing again."*

That distinction is the whole lesson of the last two days, so it belongs in the code rather than in my head.

## Where Section 16 stands

Verified end to end on real frames. `[16.1]` produces:

| | spacing | n | side | window needs | pulses | command |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REF** | 140 nm | 16 | 2.10 µm | 1.30 µm ✓ | 256 | 4° |
| **OVER** | 70 nm | 28 | 1.89 µm | 1.30 µm ✓ | 784 | 4° |

Density ratio exactly **4.0×**, template period 1.0 Λ for both, mean V +0.000000, travel overhead 1.24×, **1040 pulses ≈ 21.5 min of writing**. The 10 µm → 12 µm escalation path fired and re-took the baselines; the placement search found a worst-panel lead of 0.247 against a 0.05 minimum; the cheap rotation sense was chosen with the alternative cost printed.

## To run

`[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[16.1]` → `[16.2]` with `RUN = 1`, then set `RUN = 2` and repeat. ~33 min per run, two runs for two replicates with positions swapped.

Before each write, the four things to read in `[16.1]`: the three streak indices, the placement search's worst-case lead, whether all three baselines agree on each panel's dominant director, and `side` vs `window needs` per panel.

Two caveats I'd rather state than have you discover: the layout envelope is computed from the worst-case command angle, which is what forced the 12 µm frame and about 1.36× more pulses than the ideal — unavoidable, since positions must be fixed before commands are known. And a single run cannot separate condition from position; that's precisely how C38 went wrong, so the verdict needs both runs.

Five things surfaced only because the cells were exercised offline against real frames rather than shipped:

5. **The verdict blamed the write for a measurement failure** — now separated.

So the gate is now **line tracking** (≥ 90 %), with the offset reported and used only to decide whether re-centring is worth one more frame, at a 22 kHz trigger.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T14:19:00

**Keep the silicon probe.** The data says it's healthy, and switching now would cost you more than it buys.

## The probe is not degrading

Across 38 frames and six write sections (~4,000 pulses), the 256-px frames show:

| | first three | last three | |
|---|---|---|---|
| \|A\| | 25.7 pm | 26.0 pm | **101 %** |
| \|S\| | 32.6 | 34.0 | **104 %** |
| r12 | 0.89 | 0.94 | improving |

And the most recent frames are the **best of the whole session** — 0043–0045 gave \|A\| 43.9 / 57.0 / 57.8 pm and \|S\| up to 48.6.

I need to correct something I said last turn. I flagged "\|A\| = 23.9 pm against a campaign-healthy 50–70 pm" as a warning sign. That was a bad comparison: 23.9 pm was the **VDART** number, while LDART 256-px frames have run 15–33 pm all session. There's no decline. Disregard that flag.

A second artefact worth knowing: the 64-px frames read systematically **higher** \|A\| (34–58 pm) than 256-px frames (16–33 pm) — a bandwidth effect, not probe health. One more way the probe frame was misleading.

## Three reasons diamond would cost you

**It would invalidate r_eff = 625 nm (C11).** Conductive-diamond tips are typically 50–100 nm radius against ~20–30 nm for Pt/Ir-coated Si. Every density conclusion — C34, C37, the 50–70 % threshold — is expressed relative to Λ/2 spacing, and what plausibly sets that threshold is the halo-overlap ratio (r_eff/spacing)². Change r_eff and you're **re-measuring C34, not extending it.**

**The contact resonance would move.** `DART_NOM` is 650 kHz LDART / 350 kHz VDART at ±200 kHz. Diamond cantilevers are stiffer, so the contact resonance shifts — possibly outside those bands, and every tune, `dart_band` check and `tune_here` gate would need re-deriving.

**Mid-Section-16 is the worst possible moment.** RUN 1 vs RUN 2 *is* the replication. I built position balancing into it specifically so condition and position can be separated; swapping probes between the runs would add a probe confound on top and reproduce exactly the failure mode that made C38 a C-grade.

## The one argument for diamond, and when to act on it

The single most expensive failure of this campaign was **C22 — probe #3 stopped injecting DC** while still coupling AC at 650 kHz. That's coating delamination: the Pt/Ir wears through, the film passes 650 kHz and blocks DC, and every null becomes uninterpretable. It voided R4 and the Step 3 seed, ~70 min of instrument time. Diamond is bulk boron-doped with no coating to lose, so it's immune to that specific mode.

So diamond is the right call when the campaign moves to **large-area or long continuous writes** — where cumulative contact time makes delamination likely — but budget about an hour to re-establish r_eff and the DART bands first, and treat post-switch density results as a separate series.

## What I'd do instead, right now

Run **`[WGATE]`** before RUN 2. It's six isolated pulses plus one VDART frame, ~6 min, and it's the positive control that would have caught C22 immediately. `FINDINGS.md` §5 item 8 records that Sections 6–15 all ran without it and that it's been luck. Cheap insurance at exactly the point where you'd otherwise be guessing about the tip.

Your run looks alive, incidentally — **0046 and 0047** landed at 10:09 and 10:14, both 256 px at (−10, +30), so `[16.1]` is taking its baselines with the folder fix in place.
