**Yes — go straight to RUN 2. You don't need `[WGATE]`, because RUN 1 already *is* a positive control, and a better one.**

## RUN 1 worked, and worked well

Λ = 325 nm here. Both panels started dominant at **64°** with near-identical leads (−0.259, −0.290) — so the per-panel command fix did its job: **the tasks really were matched this time.**

| panel | spacing | pulses | dom before → after | lead after | vs floor | w(cmd) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REF** Λ/2 | 163 nm | 256 | 64° → **4°** | +0.088 | **4.0×** | 0.452 |
| **OVER** Λ/4 | 81 nm | 576 | 64° → **4°** | **+0.726** | **11.8×** | **0.831** |

```
REF    w(4) 0.300->0.452   w(64) 0.560->0.184   w(124) 0.140->0.364
OVER   w(4) 0.301->0.831   w(64) 0.591->0.104   w(124) 0.108->0.065
```

A tip that turns the superdomains through 60° at 4.0× and 11.8× the control floor is unambiguously injecting charge. `[WGATE]` tests something *weaker* — out-of-plane switching at six isolated sites — so it could only confirm what this frame already proves. Skipping it is the right call.

## What RUN 1 hints, and why RUN 2 still matters

On a genuinely matched task, **over-drive looks better on every measure**: d(lead) +1.017 vs +0.347 (2.9×), w(cmd) 0.831 vs 0.452, and **per-pulse 1.77 vs 1.36 per 1000** — so Λ/4 is ahead even after paying 2.25× the pulses. That reverses the confounded Section 15 reading, which suggested over-drive was *worse* per pulse.

One detail worth noting: REF reached the command but messily — it drained w(64°) from 0.560 to 0.184 and split it between 4° **and 124°** (which rose to 0.364). OVER drove almost everything into the command and depleted both other directors. So Λ/4 isn't just stronger, it's cleaner.

But this is n = 1 per condition, and REF sat left while OVER sat right. That's exactly the condition-versus-position confound that made C38 a C-grade. **RUN 2 swaps them**, and that's the whole point.

## Two things to fix before you launch RUN 2

**The RUN 2 default offset was wrong.** `(14, 30)` comes within 12.0 µm of S15 at (26, 28) where 12.5 is required at the worst-case 12 µm frame — the guard would have refused after taking baselines. I've changed the default to **(−22, 30)**: same y, so only x moves and the drift regime matches RUN 1, and it clears everything. `(−10, 42)` is the fallback if the material at x = −22 turns out poor. I also corrected the guard's record of RUN 1 to (−10, 30) rather than the (0, 30) originally planned.

**Note the three-baseline fix earned its keep.** Of your four pre-write frames, only 0048 was both 100 % tracked and strong (\|S\| 42.0, r12 +0.95). 0046 and 0047 tracked 86 % and 75 %, and **0049 was a bad frame** — \|S\| 15.1, r12 +0.82, offset 27.6 kHz, the same signature as the one that voided Section 14. `pick_ref` correctly chose 0048. With two baselines this could easily have gone the other way.

One caveat on the floor: the director flipped in **3 of 12** untouched tiles (25 %), right at my usability threshold. All three were tiles whose populations were nearly tied (leads +0.038, −0.123, +0.012), where a flip means little — but if RUN 2's flip rate comes out higher, treat the comparison with more caution.

The probe, incidentally, is still fine: VDART after RUN 1 gives 36.4/63.6 % with the gate open, and \|S\| = 40.2 on the after-frame, in line with the whole session.

## RUN 2, and the verdict on over-drive

Λ = 300 nm, both panels started dominant at 60°, both commanded to 0°, positions swapped from RUN 1. Control: **0 of 12** untouched tiles changed director, Δlead +0.033 ± 0.052.

| run | | pulses | dom | lead after | vs floor | **w(cmd)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | REF Λ/2 (left) | 256 | 64→**4°** | +0.088 | 4.0× | 0.452 |
| 1 | OVER Λ/4 (right) | 576 | 64→**4°** | +0.726 | 11.8× | **0.831** |
| 2 | OVER Λ/4 (left) | 576 | 60→**0°** | +0.758 | 9.8× | **0.861** |
| 2 | REF Λ/2 (right) | 256 | 60→**0°** | +0.302 | 7.2× | 0.599 |

**4/4 turned.** On final purity the conditions separate with no overlap: OVER 0.831/0.861 against REF 0.452/0.599 — a gap of **+0.232** against a within-condition scatter of 0.147. Λ/4 is also far more reproducible (spread 0.030 vs 0.147).

One honest qualification: on Δ(lead) the gap (+0.116) is *smaller* than the scatter (0.554), because REF's Δ depended strongly on where it started. **w(commanded) — the final state — is the sound metric**, and it's also the one that matches what we actually want. Per-pulse efficiency is not resolved: RUN 1 favours OVER by 1.3×, RUN 2 favours REF by 1.65×.

---

# The theory

## What the results force

Two things had to change.

**First, the symmetry statement that was missing.** PZTO(111) has three mechanical skeletons related by 120° rotation about [111]. **A uniform out-of-plane field is invariant under that rotation**, so by symmetry it *cannot* lift the three-fold degeneracy. It can inject energy and disorder the texture, but it can never select a director.

That is C8 — "every write disorders the local orientation; none rotates it" — explained rather than described. Weeks of ladders, AC melts and orbit-gate work were all uniform-E_z perturbations, and none of them could have worked. Doc 3's "orbit purity forecloses in-plane control" (P4) was the wrong diagnosis of a real obstruction.

To select a skeleton, the perturbation must carry a **direction**. A charge-balanced pulse lattice supplies one **as a wavevector, not as a field polarity** — which explains why charge balance protects the out-of-plane orbit (C13, and again at 4× density in S16) while the *pattern* sets the in-plane director, and why flipping every sign would change nothing.

**Second, the drive and the selection rule are separate conditions.** This is what killed T2. I predicted P50 ≈ full effect because dropping columns preserves the template period exactly. It does — and P50 still gave 2 % of full. The selection rule was intact; the *drive* was gone.

## T3 — commensurate templating with a ferroelastic threshold

The order parameter is not the polarization. It is **which of three ferroelastic twin skeletons occupies a region** — a three-state Potts variable with C₃ᵥ symmetry, whose lamellar period Λ is set by elastic-vs-wall energy.

Each skeleton carries an intrinsic P_z modulation at wavevector **Q** = (2π/Λ)·n̂⊥ — that's C16, the write polarity reversing eight times inside one superdomain. A patterned field E_z(**r**) couples to it as −∫P_z E_z, which is nonzero **only when q = Q**. So:

> **Condition 1 — selection (directional).** The template must be commensurate with the lamellae in both period and direction. This decides *which* director. It survives thinning at fixed period.
>
> **Condition 2 — drive (amplitude).** Converting skeleton A→B is a ferroelastic transformation: nucleate and sweep twin walls against elastic misfit and pinning. The barrier is a **local areal energy**, so the driving areal charge density must exceed a critical value. This decides *whether anything happens* — and it is blind to how the sites are arranged.

## The test: one number, nineteen panels

If Condition 2 is a local areal energy, then

σ = (1/spacing²) × keep-fraction × V × dwell  [V·s/µm²]

should separate every success from every failure in the campaign. It does:

```
 146  S12 dose 20%   FAILED   went to the wrong director
 255  S13 P50        FAILED   stayed put
 255  S13 R50        FAILED   wrong director
 255  S13 W50        FAILED   tie
 292  S12 dose 40%   FAILED   lead +0.017
------------------------------- sigma_c = 302 +- 9 -------------------------------
 311  S14 70%        turned
 356  S14 80%        turned
 376  S16a REF       turned
 400  S14 90%        turned
 444  S14 100%       turned      444  S16b REF   turned
 510  S13 FULL       turned      510  S15 REF    turned
 731  S12 size 1.29  turned     1524  S16a OVER  turned
1778  S16b OVER      turned     2041  S15 OVER   held
```

**14 successes above, 5 failures below, no overlap** — across four sections, five areas, two probes, Λ from 234 to 325 nm, panel sizes 1.3–2.5 µm, and every thinning geometry we tried. **σ_c = 302 ± 9 V·s/µm².**

And the three 50 % arms of Section 13 — thinned along the stripes, across them, and at random — sit at *identical* σ = 255 with *identical* outcomes. That is Condition 2 being a scalar areal quantity, not a Fourier one.

Above threshold the final purity is **logarithmic** in drive: w(cmd) = 0.234·ln σ − 0.887, **r = +0.974** over the four S16 panels, extrapolating to w → 1 at about 10 σ_c.

## Where T3 is weak — one problem I can't yet solve

r_eff = 625 nm against spacings of 70–163 nm, so **the halo is 4–9 times the lattice spacing.** If the coupling were to a *smoothed* field, the Fourier amplitude at q = 2π/Λ would be suppressed by exp(−q²r_eff²/2) with q·r_eff ≈ 13 — utterly negligible. Yet commensuration demonstrably works.

So the pattern information must survive the halo by some route I don't have: the halo is plausibly a **nucleation footprint** rather than a field kernel, or selection happens locally at each pulse rather than through a time-averaged field. This is T3's weakest joint and I'd rather name it than paper over it.

Second caveat: σ_c is fitted to the data it explains, and the 19 panels share areas and probes. It is not yet a prediction. Third: σ lumps V with dwell, but C21's ~40 V·s single-pulse threshold suggests they aren't freely interchangeable — note that at 10 V·s per site the lattice works *collectively*, four times below the single-pulse threshold.

---

# Hypotheses

**H6 — the threshold is in areal energy, not in site count.** σ is the variable, so a 50 % lattice at **2 s** dwell (σ = 444) should work where 50 % at 1 s (σ = 222) failed three times over. *This is the decisive test of T3's central claim, and if it holds it reopens the cost question: fewer, stronger pulses.*

**H7 — selection is resonant in Λ, not merely directional.** Every lattice we have written had sign period exactly Λ. At fixed sites, fixed σ and fixed direction, changing only the sign map to give period 2Λ should **fail**. If it succeeds, only the lattice's *axis* matters and Condition 1 is much weaker than T3 says.

**H8 — strain alone should select.** If the order parameter is ferroelastic, an anisotropic in-plane strain should choose a skeleton with no charge at all. A **zero-bias high-load raster** along a director is a one-panel test that discriminates elastic from electrostatic selection.

**H9 — commanding 30° must give a two-phase mixture, not a 30° texture.** 30° is not an allowed state. The three-state Potts symmetry predicts the population splits roughly equally between the two flanking directors. A continuous-response picture predicts a peak at 30°.

**H10 — retention should scale with how far above threshold you drove.** More drive leaves more walls pinned, so the Λ/4 panels (w ≈ 0.85) should relax *fractionally less* than the Λ/2 panels (w ≈ 0.52). Free — just re-image the two S16 areas at +1 h and +4 h.

---

# Experimental plan

## Section 17 — the 2 × 2 that tests both conditions at once (priority)

Four panels at spacing Λ/2 in one frame, same commanded director, chosen per panel:

| | sign period | keep | dwell | σ | tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Λ | 100 % | 1 s | 444 | positive control |
| **B** | Λ | 50 % | **2 s** | 444 | **H6** |
| **C** | **2Λ** | 100 % | 1 s | 444 | **H7** |
| **D** | Λ | 50 % | 1 s | 222 | negative control (replicates S13) |

768 pulses, **~17 min of writing**. A clean factorial: σ above/below × on/off resonance, with the count-vs-charge trade crossing it.

- **A turns, B turns, C fails, D fails** → T3 confirmed in both conditions. Count and charge are interchangeable; commensuration is required.
- **B fails** → σ is the wrong variable; site density matters in itself, and T3's Condition 2 needs replacing.
- **C turns** → commensuration is not required, only the lattice axis. Condition 1 collapses to a much weaker directional rule — and Λ-matching, which we've enforced everywhere, was never necessary.

## Then, in order

**Section 18 — H8, strain-only selection.** One zero-bias high-load raster panel plus a bias-matched control. If strain selects, the whole mechanism is elastic and the electrostatic framing is wrong — which would be the biggest single revision available and it costs one frame.

**Section 19 — H9, the 30° command.** Two panels at 30° and one at 0° as reference. Tests the Potts symmetry directly.

**H10 costs nothing** — fold the retention re-images into whatever runs next.

I'd hold **H6/H7 (Section 17) as the immediate next run**: it's cheap, it's a factorial with its own internal controls, and every outcome discriminates. Want me to build it?

T3 splits the lattice's action into two independent conditions — commensuration (which director) and areal drive (whether anything happens). Testing the second on existing data gave the result I didn't expect to be so clean:

| | period | keep | dwell | σ | σ/σ_c | tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Two things I put guards on. And the write is capped on **time** rather than pulse count, since dwell now varies.

`[17.2]` prints the 2×2 truth table and branches to a named conclusion for each outcome — including "σ is not the drive variable" if B fails, which would mean the 19-panel threshold was keep-fraction masquerading as σ, and "commensuration not required" if C turns, which would mean matching Λ was never necessary in any section.

The dry run caught a real inefficiency. Here's the state of Section 17.

## The design logic verified

```
      period   keep  dwell  V.s/site   sigma  x sigma_c   expect
A      1.0 L   100%    1.0      10.0     511       1.69     TURN
B      1.0 L    50%    2.0      20.0     511       1.69     TURN
C      2.0 L   100%    1.0      10.0     511       1.69       no
D      1.0 L    50%    1.0      10.0     256       0.85       no
```

**A, B and C carry identical σ = 511**, each differing from A in exactly one factor; D drops below threshold on resonance. The assertion enforcing that σ match passed, the per-pulse charge check passed (20 V·s at panel B, half C21's 40 V·s single-pulse threshold), charge balance is exact per panel, and `mean V +0.000000` overall.

## The inefficiency, and the fix

**n came out 20, not 16 — 1200 pulses and 32.1 min, over the cap.**

The cause is structural, and the same one that cost Section 16 a frame-size step: the layout envelope must be conservative, because positions and halo clearances are fixed *before* any command is known, so it assumes the widest command (factor 1.388 at 124° against 1.067 at 4°). But every panel then picks the *cheapest* command — so sizing on 1.388 over-builds all four.

`n` doesn't enter σ, so re-sizing can't disturb the factorial; it only changes written area and pulse count, and C32 says the order parameter is size-independent over 1.3–2.5 µm. `[17.1]` now re-solves `N_SIDE` from the commands actually chosen, asserts each panel's side still holds its window at *its own* angle, and raises if the envelope turns out not to have been conservative. That recovers **768 pulses, ~20 min** when the commands are cheap, and it degrades gracefully to 1200 when they aren't.

Worth noting the general lesson, since it's now bitten twice: **any quantity fixed before the commands are known has to assume the worst angle, and any quantity fixed afterwards should not.** Positions and halos belong to the first group, panel size to the second.

## Cost

**768 pulses, 14.9 min of dwell, ~20 min of writing** with the 1.37× travel overhead, ~36 min total. Offset **(−10, 42)**, clear of all eleven prior areas at the worst-case 12 µm frame.

## Run order

`[TOOLKIT]` → `[WRAPPERS]` → `[17.1]` → `[17.2]`, cells **84–85**.

Before letting `[17.2]` write, the things worth reading in `[17.1]`: the three streak indices, the placement search's worst-case lead, that all three baselines agree on each panel's dominant director, the σ table showing A/B/C identical, the re-sizing line, and `mean V +0.000000`.

I'll confirm when the re-run lands. The pre-registered predictions are printed by the cell itself, so the verdict in `[17.2]` can't be reverse-engineered after the fact — which matters here, because I've already had one theory (T2) fail by my fitting the interpretation to the result.

## Where this leaves the theory

The whole point of this run is that **every outcome is informative**, and the predictions are printed by the cell before the write so the verdict can't be back-fitted:

- **A✓ B✓ C✗ D✗** → T3 holds in both conditions. Count trades against charge, commensuration is required, and the cost question reopens — the next step would push the trade to 25 % × 4 s to find where it breaks.
- **B✗** → σ isn't the drive variable and the 19-panel threshold was keep-fraction masquerading as σ. Condition 2 needs replacing, and the follow-up is to vary V at fixed dwell and spacing, which moves σ without moving the count.
- **C✓** → commensuration isn't required, only the lattice axis. Matching Λ, which every section has enforced, was never necessary — and that would simplify the recipe considerably.
- **D✓** → σ_c is area-dependent, or 302 was overfitted to data it was derived from.

That last risk is worth keeping in view: σ_c = 302 ± 9 is a fit to the 19 panels it explains, and those panels share areas and probes. Section 17 is the first chance for it to make a prediction rather than a retrodiction.

I'd also still flag T3's weakest joint, unchanged by this build: r_eff = 625 nm is 4–9× the lattice spacing, so a smoothed field would have essentially no Fourier amplitude at q = 2π/Λ, yet commensuration demonstrably works. If C fails as predicted, that tension becomes the main thing the theory owes an explanation for.

## The audit

Every area already written is legal. **Section 17 was the only violation**, and it hadn't run yet:

| area | offset | size | \|x\|+L | \|y\|+L | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S14 | (+26, +15) | 12 | 38.0 | 27.0 | ok |
| S15 | (+26, +28) | 12 | 38.0 | 40.0 | ok |
| S16 r1 | (−10, +30) | 10 | 20.0 | 40.0 | ok |
| S16 r2 | (−22, +30) | 10 | 32.0 | 40.0 | ok |
| **S17 as built** | **(−10, +42)** | **12** | 22.0 | **54.0** | **VIOLATION** |

Its frame edge would have landed at y = +48 — technically 2 µm inside on the generous reading, which is not a margin worth having at a hard stop.

## Fixes

**Section 17 moved to (−34, 30).** Twelve µm of stage travel from the S16 RUN 2 position, |x|+L = 46, |y|+L = 42, and clear of all eleven earlier areas at the worst-case frame. I searched the legal box — 803 positions satisfy both constraints, and this is the nearest to where the tip already is.

**`scanner_ok()` added to the toolkit and wired into `[13.1]`, `[14.1]`, `[15.1]`, `[16.1]`, `[17.1]`.** It checks the **largest candidate frame**, not the nominal one, because `FRAME_TRY` escalates when Λ is coarse — which is exactly how this slipped past: I'd been reasoning about 10 µm while the guard chain assumes 12. It enforces |offset| + size ≤ 50 and reports both that and where the frame edge physically lands, so if you ever want to work closer to the limit you can see precisely what you're choosing.

It sits immediately after the footprint guard, so both position checks happen before the tune — a second, not a scan.

## Notebook state

**167 cells, syntax all OK.** Section 17 at cells 84–86, offset (−34, 30), 768 pulses, ~20 min of writing.

One thing this makes me want to flag: `scanner_ok` closes a gap that had been open through eleven areas purely by luck — the campaign drifted outward in y from 0 to 30 µm over the session, and 42 was simply the next step in that pattern. If you plan to keep working outward, the remaining legal room at a 12 µm frame is |offset| ≤ 38 in each axis, so there's about one more ring of areas available before the sample needs repositioning under the head.

## Where we stand

Today closed the over-drive question (Λ/4 reaches w = 0.83–0.86 against Λ/2's 0.45–0.60, positions swapped, 4/4 turned) and produced the campaign's first quantitative law — **σ_c = 302 ± 9 V·s/µm² separating all 19 panels written so far**, with a logarithmic saturation above it.

Section 17 is the first chance for that number to make a *prediction* rather than a retrodiction, and it tests the two halves of T3 independently: whether the drive variable is really areal charge density (B), and whether commensuration with Λ is really required (C). Both predictions are printed by the cell before the write, so the verdict can't be back-fitted — which matters, because T2 died precisely from my fitting an interpretation to a result.

Three things I'd keep on the list, in rough priority:

**T3's unresolved joint.** r_eff = 625 nm is 4–9× the lattice spacing, so a smoothed field would carry essentially no Fourier amplitude at q = 2π/Λ — yet commensuration works. If C fails as predicted, explaining that becomes the theory's main debt.

**Q14, unscreened.** C23, C29 and C30 all used commands near 0° in some panels, and none of their frames were checked for the streak artefact that nearly voided Section 14. `streak_index()` is cheap and those conclusions are load-bearing.

**The VDART drift.** Minority fraction has gone 46.0 → 36.4 → 33.0 % across the last three areas with |⟨e^iφ⟩| rising 0.390 → 0.437 → 0.493. Those are different areas so it may be spatial rather than cumulative, but if Section 17 continues the trend it's worth taking seriously as slow out-of-plane poling.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T17:12:55

The efficiency question has a concrete answer, and it isn't "use small frames".

## Why smaller frames don't help

**Frame time is `px / rate` — independent of scan size.** A 256-px frame at 1 Hz takes 4.27 min whether it scans 6 µm or 16 µm. So the imaging overhead of an iteration (tune-verify + 2 baselines + after + VDART = **21 min**) is *fixed*, and a small frame just spreads it over fewer conditions:

| frame | grid | conditions | **min per condition** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6–8 µm | 1×1 | 1 | **24–27** |
| 10 µm | 2×2 | 4 | **8.8** |
| **12 µm** | **3×2** | **6** | **7.7** |
| 14 µm | 3×3 | 9 | 6.2 |

Both scalings favour larger frames — imaging per condition goes as pitch²/size, and *tip sliding* per condition goes as 1/size. The binding constraint is the **write budget**, not the frame.

Two hard limits do appear, and both are now computed rather than assumed:

**The pixel crossover.** Above `frame ≈ 0.0413 × Λ[nm]` µm, the readout window becomes pixel-limited instead of Λ-limited, panels grow, and the gain stops. At Λ = 300 nm that's **12.4 µm** — exactly where the table stops improving cleanly. At Λ = 234 it's 9.7 µm; at Λ = 388, 16.0 µm.

**Tip speed.** `rate` is now scaled to hold tip speed at **20 µm/s** — the 10 µm / 1 Hz condition — so a 12 µm frame runs at 0.83 Hz rather than sliding 24 µm/s. That's the same discipline as removing the 40 µm/s probe frame.

## The physics constraint that makes large frames safe

**Λ moved 10–15 % per 10 µm** across today's areas (234 → 280 → 300 → 325 nm). In a 12 µm frame a frame-average Λ would mis-set the Λ/2 spacing for outlying panels — and if commensuration matters (T3's Condition 1), that's the difference between testing it and confounding it.

`lambda_uniformity()` now measures Λ **at each panel position** and each panel's spacing comes from its own local value, with a warning above 15 % spread. Without this, packing more panels per frame would quietly corrupt the experiment.

## What's in `autoloop.py` — 796 lines

`plan_iteration()` (the table above), `lambda_uniformity()`, `solve_dose()` (targets σ/σ_c and solves the recipe from measured Λ, holding period = Λ and per-site charge under half the C21 threshold), `current_offset()` / `check_area_fresh()` (reads where you moved rather than choosing), `legal_offsets()`, `preflight()` (S1–S28 as code), `read_direction()`, `refine_sigma_c()`, `log_to_notebook()`, `remind()`, and the Igor lock.

Plus `PITFALLS.md` at 661 lines with §6 (direction), §8 (safety envelope S1–S29) and §9 (loop protocol); `FINDINGS.md` at 1165 lines with C39–C40; and a memory file so the goal survives compaction.

## Default plan going forward

**12 µm, 6 conditions, ~0.6 s mean dwell → 21 min write, 46 min total, 7.7 min per condition** — against Section 17's 4 conditions at 10.3 min each. About **25 % more information per minute of instrument time and per unit of tip travel.**

## IT1 — the T3 factorial plus the σ_c prediction, one 12 µm frame

Five written panels on a 3×2 grid, plus the sixth slot left **unwritten as an in-grid control** — same scan history as the panels, which is a better control than edge bands alone.

| | target | period | keep | dwell | V·s/site | σ | pulses | tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | 1.50 σ_c | Λ | 100 % | 1.00 s | 10.0 | 444 | 256 | positive control, factorial reference |
| **B** | 1.50 σ_c | Λ | **50 %** | **2.00 s** | 20.0 | 444 | 128 | **Q15** — is σ the drive variable? |
| **C** | 1.50 σ_c | **2Λ** | 100 % | 1.00 s | 10.0 | 444 | 256 | **Q16** — is commensuration required? |
| **D** | 0.70 σ_c | Λ | 99 % | 0.48 s | 4.8 | 211 | 254 | below threshold, negative control |
| **E** | **1.00 σ_c** | Λ | 100 % | 0.68 s | 6.8 | 302 | 256 | **the prediction test** |

**A, B and C carry identical σ = 444** and each differs from A in exactly one factor. D and E bracket σ_c from below and sit on it — and E is the first time σ_c has been asked to *predict* rather than retrodict.

**1150 pulses, 23.9 min of writing, 47 min total, 9.4 min per condition.** It answers three open questions in one frame where Section 17 addressed two in a 10 µm frame at 10.3 min each.

## Efficiency, as you asked

- **12 µm at 0.83 Hz** — rate scaled so tip speed stays at 20 µm/s, the same condition as 10 µm at 1 Hz. No extra sliding rate.
- **Six slots instead of four**, because the imaging overhead is fixed per iteration regardless of frame size.
- **VDART at 128 px** — orbit balance doesn't need Λ resolution, saving 2.6 min.
- Dwell is varied at near-full density rather than thinning, which also makes E's threshold test independent of how σ_c was originally fitted (mostly on density).

Honest limit: IT1 is **write-dominated** because the factorial needs σ comfortably above threshold, and that costs dwell. The efficiency gains land harder in later iterations where σ is fixed and short.

## Two things the design does that earlier sections didn't

**Every dose is re-solved from the LOCAL Λ at each panel.** Λ moved 10–15 % per 10 µm across today's areas, so a frame-average would put the outlying panels off resonance — which for panel C is the difference between testing commensuration and confounding it.

**The offset in the proposal is a placeholder.** The loop reads the stage position at build time and verifies it's clear of all 12 used areas and inside the scanner range. 764 legal positions remain for a 12 µm frame.

## Before I start, three things I need from you

1. **Move to the fresh area** and leave the stage there — I'll read the position rather than choose it.
2. **Confirm your Jupyter kernel is idle** and won't run instrument cells. aespm drives Igor through a command file; if your kernel and the loop both write to it the commands interleave. I take `autoloop.lock`, but that only protects against a second loop, not against your kernel.
3. **Say go.** Then I'll take the lock, verify the folder and position, tune, take three baselines, check texture and streaks, build against the measured Λ, write, read, and log the iteration into the notebook with its motivation, pre-registered prediction and result.

To stop me at any point: create a file named `STOP` in the project directory. The loop checks for it before every write.

One caveat I'd rather state now: I'm assuming S17 failed for a reason that doesn't recur — if it failed because that *area* had no texture, IT1 will catch it at the modulation check (< 0.10 aborts before writing) and I'll report rather than push on.

**IT1 is running.** Preflight passed clean and the loop has the lock.

## What it's doing

At **(0, 0), 12 µm, 256 px, 0.83 Hz** — rate set so tip speed stays at 20 µm/s.

Sequence: folder + range + footprint + idle checks → tune verified on a full-resolution frame (which becomes baseline 1) → two more baselines → `pick_ref` with the r12 gate → streak screen → triad pinned to `FAM_FILM` → **modulation gate** → local Λ at each of six slots → per-panel command 60° from that panel's own dominant director → dwell solved per panel so A/B/C hit identical σ despite different local Λ → build with every assertion → write → after-frame → direction readout → VDART at 128 px.

| | target | period | keep | tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | 1.50 σ_c | Λ | 100 % | positive control |
| **B** | 1.50 σ_c | Λ | 50 %, 2× dwell | **is σ the drive variable?** |
| **C** | 1.50 σ_c | **2Λ** | 100 % | **is commensuration required?** |
| **D** | 0.70 σ_c | Λ | 100 % | below threshold |
| **E** | **1.00 σ_c** | Λ | 100 % | **the σ_c prediction** |
| **G** | — | — | unwritten | in-grid control |

**~47 min**: 23 min imaging, 24 min writing.

## It will stop itself rather than push on

The run aborts before writing if: the folder is stale, (0,0) isn't clear, a frame landed in the last 2 min, the reference frame is streaky above 0.10, **modulation is below 0.10** (no texture to rotate), any slot has no clear dominant director, the A/B/C σ spread exceeds 8 %, write time exceeds 26 min, charge balance fails, or a `STOP` file appears. That last one is your kill switch — `STOP` in the project directory.

If the readout comes back unreadable it records a **strike, not a result**, and says so — the panels persist and can be re-scored from fresh baselines.

## One thing I changed on your answer

The coarse-stage move means the twelve recorded areas refer to the *previous* sample position, so I archived them and reset the footprint table rather than carrying them forward — they'd have blocked good positions for no reason and permitted bad ones. The film triad should carry over (C31 has it constant across eight areas) but Λ is being re-measured, and every dose derives from it.

I'll report when it lands: the direction table, whether σ_c predicted in a fresh area, and what it does to T3. The iteration gets logged into the notebook with its motivation, the pre-registered prediction, and the result — and `FINDINGS.md` gets whatever survives.

## What happened

It cleared every guard — folder, scanner range, footprint at the reset table, idle check — tuned successfully, then died on its **first frame**:

```
AttributeError: 'Experiment' object has no attribute 'check_files'
```

`frame()` calls `exp.check_files()`, which the notebook attaches to the Experiment object in **cell 25** via `add_func`. My `load_toolkit` only exec'd the library, toolkit and wrapper cells, so the real Experiment came up bare. Fixed by attaching `check_files`, `read_meter` and `load_ibw` when the live object is built, with an assertion that it took.

**Nothing was written and no frame landed** — the file count is unchanged at 68, newest still `LDART_0060` from 12:57. I issued a `Stop` to clear the scan `frame()` had started, and confirmed the lock was released by the `finally` block.

Two things worth noting about the failure mode, since they're the reason this was cheap rather than expensive:

**The failure came before the write, not during it.** The sequence deliberately puts the tune and all three baselines ahead of any pulse, so a tooling error costs a tune rather than a sample area. That ordering is why this cost ~6 minutes.

**The `finally` block released the lock.** Otherwise the next launch would have refused with a stale lock, and I'd have had to decide whether it was safe to delete — exactly the ambiguity the lock exists to prevent.

## A gap in my own dry-running

I verified `load_toolkit(stub_instrument=True)` extensively and never verified `stub_instrument=False`, because that path talks to the instrument. So the one code path that matters for autonomous running was the one I couldn't test offline. I've now made it assert rather than fail late, but the general lesson belongs in `PITFALLS.md` — I'll add it: *the stubbed and live paths differ, so verify what you can about the live path (attribute presence, signatures) without executing it.*

The run is going again from the top: tune → three baselines → `pick_ref` → streak screen → triad and modulation gate → local Λ per slot → per-panel commands → doses solved from local Λ → write → readout → VDART. About 47 minutes.

I'll report the direction table and what it does to T3 when it lands.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T17:47:23

**IT1 running again**, third attempt. Both earlier failures were tooling, both halted before any write, and I've verified the whole path offline against the real reference frame this time.

## What the two halts found

**Attempt 2** halted at `slot (0.93,4.10) halo leaves the frame` — correctly. The layout sized panels for the *worst possible* command angle (126°, factor 1.397) because positions must be fixed before commands are known, which inflated the pitch to 5.07 µm so three columns needed 15.1 µm in a 12 µm frame.

This is the **third** time worst-angle sizing has bitten: it escalated Section 16's frame, built n = 20 where 16 sufficed in Section 17, and now halted IT1. So I fixed the pattern rather than the instance — placement is now a **fixed point**: provisional layout on the cheapest director, read the commands it implies, re-size on those, repeat until the angle set stops growing.

That immediately paid for itself by finding something real. The 3×2 grid **doesn't settle here**: the fifth slot's own dominant director is 6°, so its command must be 66°, which pushes the factor to 1.316 where three columns don't fit. Genuine spatial variation in the texture — exactly why commands are chosen per panel. It falls back to a **2×2**, which settles cleanly with all four dominants at 66° and all commands at 6°, and **drops panel E** (the σ_c prediction point), keeping the factorial and the negative control.

## And it reversed one of my own improvements

I proposed per-panel Λ two steps ago, arguing a frame average would put outlying panels off resonance. Simulating it showed the local estimate **doesn't converge at any block size** — mean drifting 217 → 337 nm as the block grows, which is an estimator artefact, not variation. Worse, the full 256-px frame already disagrees with itself across triad members: **280 / 388 / 261 nm, a 48 % spread**.

So Λ isn't a single well-determined number here. Consequences, which differ:

- **σ is unaffected** — it uses the spacing we *command*, which is exact, and the dose solver adjusts dwell to hit the target regardless.
- **Commensuration is fuzzy** — "period = Λ" is defined only to about ±30 %. Panel C's Λ-vs-2Λ contrast survives (a factor of two beats 30 %), but a fine detuning experiment would not. That's a real limit on how sharply Q16 can be answered here, and I'd rather say it now than discover it in the interpretation.

I'm halting the loop rather than starting IT2. Three things converged and one of them is about the sample, not the code.

## IT1 wrote successfully

896 pulses, 18.7 min, `mean V +0.0000`, litho ran 14:30:52 → 14:49:51 with `Stop` issued. The build was exactly as designed: 2×2, all four commands at 6° from a local dominant of 66°, **A/B/C at σ = 449.9 with 0.0 % spread**.

## But the readout is unusable, and the loop said so

**Untouched control tiles changed dominant director in 5 of 16 (31 %)**, floor 0.352 — above the 25 % gate. So it recorded a strike, not a result, and logged the iteration to the notebook as unreadable.

What makes this more than noise: **all four panels went 66° → 6°**, including **D**, the negative control at σ = 204 = 0.68 σ_c which was predicted *not* to turn — and D's Δ(lead) of +0.710 was the second largest. Either the frame drifted globally toward 6°, or something pushed the whole field. A 55-minute gap between the baselines and the after-frame is enough for real thermal drift at 12 µm, which would make control tiles sample different material and manufacture apparent director changes.

## The finding that actually concerns me

The out-of-plane orbit balance across the session:

| | minority | \|⟨e^iφ⟩\| | |
|---|---|---|---|
| after S15 | 46.0 % | 0.390 | |
| after S16 r1 | 36.4 % | 0.437 | |
| after S16 r2 | 33.0 % | 0.493 | |
| **after IT1** | **19.5 %** | **0.662** | **outside the 21–36 % reference — gate shut** |

**Monotonic across four areas, and now outside the campaign envelope.** I flagged this trend two turns ago as "worth watching if it continues"; it has continued and crossed the line. Every file has been charge-balanced to `mean V = 0.0000`, so this is not the C13 net-DC mechanism — it looks cumulative, and it survived a coarse-stage move to fresh material, which argues it's the *tip* rather than the sample.

`contact_check` on the after-frame agrees: *"MOVE TO A DIFFERENT LOCATION AND RETUNE… the contact spot itself is bad — debris or a step edge."*

## Why I'm stopping rather than continuing

If the orbit gate is shut, the population we're trying to steer is no longer in the two-class regime that C13 and the whole T3 framework assume. Writing IT2 into that state would measure a moving target, and I'd be spending your probe and sample to produce data I couldn't interpret. The protocol's two-strike rule exists for exactly this; I'd rather invoke it one strike early than accumulate an uninterpretable series.

## What I'd do, cheapest first

**Re-score IT1 without writing** — 2–3 fresh frames, ~10 min. The panels persist. If they still read 6°-dominant while the control bands read 66°, IT1 *has* a qualitative result even though the floor was too large to quantify. That's free information and it doesn't depend on resolving anything else.

**Then check the tip, not the sample.** A VDART on genuinely untouched material far from everything written: if it also reads ~20 % minority, the skew is the tip's response, not accumulated poling. That distinguishes "probe is dying" from "sample is poling" and it's one frame.

**Probe change is likely warranted.** The contact check has been escalating — it asked for a setpoint raise at 13:39 and by 14:50 was asking to move location. Combined with the orbit skew, that reads as a probe reaching end of life. This is where a diamond tip becomes worth its recalibration cost — the C22 failure mode (AC couples, DC blocked) is exactly what a worn coating does, and we'd be re-establishing r_eff and the DART bands anyway after a probe change.

Say which you'd like and I'll run it. My recommendation is the re-score first — it costs 10 minutes, needs no decisions, and tells us whether we already have IT1's answer.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T19:24:36

**Re-score running — imaging only, no writes.** About 20 minutes.

Your setpoint observation reframes the whole result, so I built the script to *measure* the artefact rather than assume it. It scores five comparisons on untouched film:

| comparison | what it isolates |
|---|---|
| fresh vs fresh (−0.8 vs −0.8) | frame-to-frame noise at one setpoint — the true floor |
| base vs fresh (−0.8 vs −0.8) | drift over 90 min at matched force |
| **base vs drifted (−0.8 vs −0.6)** | **the setpoint artefact itself** |
| drifted vs fresh (−0.6 vs −0.8) | the same artefact from the other side |

If "base vs drifted" is much worse than "base vs fresh", the 31 % flip rate was the force change and not the material. That's a direct measurement, not an inference.

Then the panels get scored **−0.8 against −0.8** — original baselines against fresh frames, contact force matched — and the VDART is repeated at the restored setpoint to see whether the 19.5 % minority that shut the gate also comes back inside the 21–36 % band.

## Why this matters beyond IT1

If the setpoint explains both, then two of my three concerns from last turn dissolve — and one of them was a conclusion I was close to drawing about the *sample*. I'd have written up "progressive out-of-plane poling across four areas, 46 → 36 → 33 → 19.5 %" as a finding. It would have been wrong, and it would have been the kind of wrong that's hard to unpick later because it fits a plausible physical story.

The general lesson belongs in `PITFALLS.md`: **the withdrawn deflection is a measurement parameter that can drift, and every before/after comparison silently assumes it didn't.** Nothing in the toolkit logs it. `contact_check` reports the *deflection setpoint* (0.60 V, unchanged) but not the withdrawn reference, so the drift was invisible to every guard I built. I'll add it to the hygiene table and to the frame log so future pairs can be checked rather than trusted.

There's also a real possibility the re-score comes back ambiguous — if D still turns alongside A, then either σ_c is much lower in this area or something drove the whole frame, and the factorial stays unreadable regardless of the setpoint. I've made the script say that explicitly rather than let me read the B-vs-C comparison out of a frame that can't support it.

I'll report the five-way artefact table, the panel verdicts, and the VDART when it lands.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T20:52:29

**IT2 running with a genuinely better metric.** This is the most substantive change since the direction fix, so it's worth being clear about what it does.

## The new primary metric

**Δ(panel − control tiles)**, where each term is measured *within a single frame*:

```
excess_after  = w(cmd)|panel  −  mean w(cmd)|tiles      both in the after-frame
excess_before = w(cmd)|panel  −  mean w(cmd)|tiles      both in the before-frame
Δexcess       = excess_after − excess_before
```

Each excess is a within-frame ratio, so global drift, gain changes, mode switches and stage hysteresis cancel inside it. Taking the difference then cancels the *spatial* bias from the tiles sitting at the frame edges while the panels sit in a row. Threshold: 2 sd of the untouched tiles in the same frame.

That replaces a floor carried across 55 minutes and several stage excursions with one built from tiles imaged in the same pass.

## What forced it

The gate's three pairwise baseline comparisons made the problem unambiguous:

| pair | floor | flips | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0079 vs 0082 | 0.511 | 57 % | separated by visits to two other areas |
| **0082 vs 0083** | **0.136** | **7 %** | **consecutive** |
| 0079 vs 0083 | 0.446 | 50 % | separated |

**The area was never the problem.** Consecutive frames sit comfortably inside the gate; the stage simply doesn't return to the same place after an excursion. I'd spent two turns blaming weak texture — modulation 0.19–0.21, Λ inconsistent — when the measurement was being broken by frame sequencing I controlled.

That also explains the IT1 re-score, where "base vs fresh" gave 0.228/19 % across a write and two mode changes while consecutive frames gave 0.139–0.181. And it means my conclusion last turn that "this region may be too weakly textured to support the metric" was wrong — I'll correct that in `FINDINGS.md` rather than leave it standing.

Seven launches, one write. Every failure has been mine, and the last two were in code I'd written *as the fix* for the previous one. ## assistant — 2026-08-21T22:05:08

IT2 produced a real result. Both panels switched, and the off-resonance one won.

## The result

Λ = 280 nm area at (−14, 0), modulation 0.210, baseline floor **0.183 with 0/14 and 7 % flips** — the area was measurable all along. σ = 600 V·s/µm² = **1.99 σ_c**, 512 pulses, 19.6 min. Both panels commanded to 2°, both starting dominant at 122°.

| | period | w(cmd) before | after | Δexcess | ×2sd | populations before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | **Λ** | 0.291 | 0.513 | +0.185 | 0.8 | 0.291→0.513 · 0.179→0.371 · **0.531→0.115** |
| **P2** | **2Λ** | 0.238 | **0.752** | **+0.477** | **2.1** | 0.238→**0.752** · 0.219→0.069 · **0.542→0.179** |

Both ended dominant at the commanded 2°, from 122°. **P2, the off-resonance panel, is 2.6× stronger than P1 on the corrected contrast and reaches w = 0.752 against 0.499.**

The second after-frame confirms it isn't a fluke of one image: P1 +0.399, P2 +0.404 — and note P1's own two after-frames disagree (+0.185 vs +0.399), which is why P1 sits near the threshold while P2 clears it in both.

## This contradicts T3's Condition 1

Identical σ, identical site positions, identical command, identical spacing — **the only difference is the sign map**, giving template period Λ versus 2Λ. If commensuration with the lamellar period were what selects, P1 should have won. It lost, and IT1's hint (panel C at 2Λ being strongest of four) now has an independent replication in a different area with a properly measured floor.

So the selecting quantity is **not** commensuration with Λ. A longer template period is better, at least at 2Λ.

That's the theory's Condition 1 falsified as written. What replaces it is open — the obvious next question is whether it keeps improving (4Λ, 8Λ) or has an optimum, and at the limit "very long period" becomes a **single sign block**, i.e. a uniform-polarity panel. If that's the best case, the whole ± template idea was wrong and what matters is the lattice *axis* plus areal density.

## The metric change is what made this readable

The withdrawn deflection drifted **−0.827 → −0.439 → −0.786** *during this run*, and the before/after floor still came out at 0.223 with 21 % flips between the two after-frames. The old metric would have called this unreadable again. The within-frame contrast, baseline-corrected for layout, gave a clean 2.1× result through that drift — which is exactly what it was built for.

## Two caveats I won't paper over

**Only 2 of 3 panels fit** — P4 (period 4Λ) was dropped when the placement settled at 2 panels, so the monotonicity question is untested. That's the single most important follow-up.

**P1 sits at 0.8× threshold on one after-frame and 1.8× on the other.** Its switch is real (dominant director moved 122° → 2°, w(cmd) 0.291 → 0.513) but its *magnitude* is uncertain. The P2 > P1 ordering is robust; the ratio is not precise.

The crash was cosmetic — I inserted the within-frame block above where `res` is defined, so the state and notebook logging didn't run. I'll fix the ordering, record C41 (period 2Λ beats Λ at matched σ) in `FINDINGS.md`, log the iteration to the notebook, and design IT3 as the period series pushed to 4Λ and 8Λ with three panels guaranteed to fit.

## assistant — 2026-08-21T22:46:12

**C41 and C42 recorded, retrospective written, IT3 running.**

## C41 — commensuration is not the selection rule · grade B

Identical σ = 600 V·s/µm², identical spacing, identical sites, identical command (2°, both from 122°). Only the sign map differed:

| | period | w(cmd) before → after | Δ(panel − tiles) | ×2sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Λ | 0.291 → 0.513 | +0.185 | 0.8 |
| **P2** | **2Λ** | 0.238 → **0.752** | **+0.477** | **2.1** |

**T3's Condition 1 is falsified.** IT1's panel C was the same ordering in a different area, so this is a replication, not a single observation. S13's W50 had looked like support for commensuration but sat at σ = 255, below threshold — period and drive were confounded there.

**C42** records the methodological fix: score panels against untouched tiles *within* one frame, baseline-corrected for layout. It also corrects my earlier claim that the region was too weakly textured — consecutive frames give a floor of 0.136–0.183; the stage simply doesn't return to the same place after an excursion.

## What went wrong, and what I changed

`PITFALLS.md` §10 now records it. Eight launches, one usable result, **six lost to my own faults** — and two of those six were introduced *by my fix for the previous one*. Two patterns:

**I discovered tooling gaps by running the instrument.** All six were statically detectable. `load_toolkit(stub_instrument=False)` is the one path I can't dry-run, and I kept accepting "it parses and the stubbed path works".

**I blamed the material before the measurement — three times.** The VDART skew (setpoint, not poling), the high floor (frame sequencing, not weak texture), the Λ spread (estimator, not the film). Each was close to being written up as physics; the poling one was monotonic across four areas and fitted a mechanism.

So IT3 has `audit_code()` running **inside the script before any instrument command** — AST scan for called-but-undefined names across every loaded cell, dangling-global check on the driver, required-name assertion in the loader. And I ran the offline simulation against real frames, which I'd been treating as optional despite it catching two real problems the one time I did it.

That simulation immediately earned its place: I'd set the frame to 10 µm for lower tip travel, and it showed the readout window becomes **pixel-limited to 26.3 px** there — barely above `dir_power`'s 24-px floor. Reverted to 12 µm where it's 1.22 µm with margin. That would have been failure number seven.

## IT3

Three panels at identical σ, differing only in sign map: **period Λ / 4Λ / 8Λ**, plus a fourth slot left unwritten as an in-grid control. `n = 16` so `sign_every = 8` still balances exactly — verified: 128 positive, 128 negative, `mean V +0.000000000` for all three.

At 8Λ the template is **two sign blocks of eight rows** — barely a lattice. If that wins, the ± template was never the mechanism and what selects is the lattice *axis* plus areal density. If 4Λ wins and 8Λ falls, there's an optimum length scale that isn't Λ. If 4Λ ≈ 8Λ, it saturates once the period exceeds the halo (r_eff = 625 nm ≈ 2.2 Λ), which would make **r_eff** the relevant scale.

On your point about getting stuck: the thing that broke the IT1/IT2 deadlock wasn't a better area or a better dose, it was **abandoning the before/after comparison** for a within-frame one that was available all along. That's now a rule in §10.4 — after two failures of the same kind, question the observable rather than the experiment.

IT3 delivered a clean result — and it **reverses the ordering IT2 found.**

## The result

Area (0, −14), Λ = 301 nm. Baseline floor **0.140 with 0/14 flips on all three pairs** — the best of the campaign. σ = 560 = 1.85 σ_c (budget-capped from 2.00, reported). All three panels commanded to 4°, all starting dominant at 64°.

| | period | w(cmd) before → after | Δ(panel − tiles) | ×2sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | **Λ** | 0.283 → **0.646** | **+0.401** | **3.1** |
| **P4** | 4Λ | 0.334 → 0.619 | +0.324 | 2.5 |
| **P8** | 8Λ | 0.335 → 0.457 | +0.161 | 1.2 |

All three switched the dominant director 64° → 4°. But the ordering is **P1 > P4 > P8** — monotonically *decreasing* with period. IT2 found the opposite (2Λ beating Λ by 2.6×).

## So C41 does not survive as stated

Three periods spanning 8× give Δexcess 0.401 / 0.324 / 0.161. The spread between P1 and P4 (0.077) is **below** the 0.129 threshold — they're indistinguishable. P8 is genuinely weaker, but at 1.2× it's marginal.

Put beside IT2's P1 = +0.185 and P2 = +0.477, the honest reading is that **panel-to-panel scatter within one area is comparable to the period effect across areas.** IT2's ordering and IT3's ordering are inconsistent, and neither is safe to build on.

What *is* consistent across IT1, IT2 and IT3: **every template period tried — Λ, 2Λ, 4Λ, 8Λ — turned the dominant director to the command.** Even 8Λ, which with n = 16 is just two sign blocks of eight rows and barely a lattice.

That's the finding, and it's stronger than either ordering: **the ± sign map is not what selects the director.** Commensuration isn't required (C41 stands on that), but neither is a longer period better. What the three iterations share is the lattice **axis** and the areal density.

I'll need to correct C41 — its grade-B claim that 2Λ beats Λ is contradicted by a better-controlled measurement in a quieter area. The replication I cited (IT1's panel C) was at 1.2–2.5× threshold in an area with a 0.23 floor, so it was never strong evidence.

**The script's verdict logic reached the right conclusion but printed the wrong header** — "IT2 VERDICT", and it also printed IT2's prediction list ("P1 best, P2 and P4 fail"). def ctrl_tiles(x0, x1, y0, y1, w_um, gap_um=0.1):
    """Square tiles across an untouched band, so the whole band is sampled.

    A floor taken from ONE box is a floor from one place. Tiling gives a spatial
    spread as well as a mean, and the spread is what caught the R12 control as
    quiet (+-0.014) and the S11 control as sitting inside the written strips.
    """
    if (y1 - y0) < w_um - 1e-9:
        raise ValueError('band is %.2f um tall but the window is %.2f um - '
                         'widen the band or shrink the window'
                         % (y1 - y0, w_um))
    yc = 0.5 * (y0 + y1)
    out, x = [], x0
    while x + w_um <= x1 + 1e-9:
        out.append((x, x + w_um, yc - w_um / 2, yc + w_um / 2))
        x += w_um + gap_um
    return out

| UP | **every site at +10 V** | 122° |
| UM | **every site at −10 V** | 122° |

Per-panel charge balance is deliberately abandoned; the *file* still cancels exactly, so there's no global DC, but each uniform panel carries a large local one and C13 predicts it re-poles out-of-plane there. That's expected, and the VDART afterwards is a required readout, not optional.

**Five defects found by simulating the real code path offline** — the thing PITFALLS §10.1 already told me to do and I hadn't been. Four had been live since IT1:

- **IT2's written area was missing from the state file.** It crashed in the verdict block before `save_state`, so `used_areas` never recorded (−14, 0) — meaning S9 and `check_area_fresh` were both blind to it and IT4 could have written straight on top. Also lost: 19.6 min from the budget, the iteration count, and the `completed` list that makes S26 able to fire at all. Repaired; the driver now commits the area immediately after the write, in its own save.
- **`preflight()` — the S1–S29 envelope as code — has never been called by any driver.** `grep -c` gives 0, 0, 0 for IT1–IT3. It crashed on `prop['offset']` being None, which every driver's design guarantees, so it was unusable for exactly the case it was written for. It now defers those groups and IT4 calls it twice; pass 2 came back all clear on the real geometry.
- **The control tiles sat on a written panel.** The upper band was built from the top edge of the *first* row, so on a 2×2 grid it began inside the second row. Audited against IT3's own frames: 3 of 14 tiles overlapped P8. Excesses move by ≤0.022 and no verdict or ordering changes — **C41 stands** — but that was luck. Tiles are now gridded and the panels subtracted, which also gained tiles (16 vs 7).
- **Tiles were read along one director while panels were read along their own** — harmless in IT3 only because all three panels shared a command.
- **Slot assignment was incidental.** UP and UM now get slots sharing a (dominant, command) by construction, so a UP−UM difference is polarity rather than starting state.

The notebook record was also inconsistent — IT3's cell was titled "ITERATION 2 … `[IT2-doc]`" and IT2 had no cell at all. Both fixed, with IT2's record reconstructed from `it2_console.txt` and marked as such.

Written up as [PITFALLS.md](PITFALLS.md) §11 and a C42 refinement in [FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md). Expect roughly 70 minutes; I'll report when the verdict lands.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T01:21:20

IT4 relaunched. The first attempt halted in placement at **zero write cost** — the guard I'd added (never write `UP` without its cancelling `UM`) fired correctly, but the arithmetic feeding it was mine:

**What went wrong.** At (0, −28) the triad is [0, 60, 120]. Three of the four 2×2 slots were dominated by 60° → command 0° (rotation factor 1.000), but the fourth was dominated by 0° → command 120° (factor 1.366). The halo is sized on the *worst* factor across the slots in use, so one awkward slot inflated n from 16 to 32 and the halo from 1.68 to 3.59 µm — nothing fit. The (2,1) fallback settled with 2 slots, and `nwrite = nslot - 1` reserved one as an in-grid control, leaving a single uniform panel, which cannot be written.

**Two faults, both mine:**

- The layout list was `((2,2), (2,1))` and **never tried a row of three**. At factor 1.000 here, 3×1 fits comfortably — three written panels were available the whole time.
- **"Keep one slot unwritten" was obsolete.** It dates from when the in-grid slot *was* the control region. Since the tile fix earlier today, controls are gridded across the frame with the written footprints subtracted, so reserving a slot buys nothing and costs a panel.

The row layout is also strictly better: σ rises to **1.99 σ_c** (from 1.85, since the halo is smaller), the write drops to 22.4 min, and the controls go from 14 tiles to **32**.

I also added a `RESUME` path rather than re-screening. The first launch spent four tunes and six frames — roughly 30 minutes of probe life — proving (0, −28) is measurable, then halted before writing anything, so the area is untouched and those frames still describe it. It reuses baselines 0103–0105 and re-checks modulation against them rather than trusting the stale number.

Simulated before relaunch: 3×1 settles on the first pass, `UP` and `UM` matched on dominant 60° → command 0° so a UP−UM difference is polarity rather than starting state, file mean V exactly 0, preflight pass 2 all clear, 32 tiles with no panel overlap.

One thing worth flagging: `contact_check` has now said *"MOVE TO A DIFFERENT LOCATION AND RETUNE — the contact spot itself is bad"* on IT2, IT3 and IT4's baselines alike, with amplitude 42–56 pm and consistency 0.85–0.87. Three areas in a row is a probe-side pattern, not a location one. It hasn't prevented readable results, so I'm not blocking on it — but if IT4 comes back muddy, the tip is where I'd look first.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T01:48:29

The threshold is now fixed, before the result — which is the point of computing it during the write:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| untouched tiles clear of all three panels | **40** |
| tile w(cmd) at command 0° | 0.241 / 0.247 / 0.243 across the three baselines |
| **2 sd threshold** | **0.190 – 0.199, mean 0.194** |
| before-term (exc0) | UP −0.035, A +0.078, UM −0.092 |
| stability of exc0 across baselines | sd ≤ 0.013 |

Two things follow, and both are worth saying now rather than after seeing which way the panels went.

**The layout-bias correction is sound.** The panel regions already differ from the tile mean before anything was written — A's region reads +0.078 high, UM's −0.092 low, a systematic x-position bias across the row. C42's subtraction removes it, and its stability to sd ≈ 0.01 across three consecutive baselines means the subtraction is reliable rather than itself a source of noise.

**This area has roughly half IT3's resolving power.** The per-tile spread is 0.097 here against 0.060 at IT3's area, so the threshold is 0.194 against IT3's 0.119. Note that more tiles does *not* help — the threshold is 2 sd of the film's own spread, not a standard error, so 40 tiles only makes the estimate of that spread precise. Concretely: transplanted here, IT3's strongest panel (+0.379) would read 2.0× threshold and its weakest (+0.139) would read 0.7× and **fail**. So the readout can see an IT3-sized effect, but a weak one will land in the unresolved band.

If UP and UM come back at 1.0–1.5× I'll say the iteration is unresolved rather than claim uniform polarity failed — a null at half the resolving power is not evidence, and PITFALLS §10.2 is four instances of me reaching for physics when the measurement was the problem. If that happens the honest next step is a sub-window analysis: each panel is 3.5 µm across and the window is 1.26 µm, so four sub-windows fit inside one panel, giving a panel mean with its own standard error instead of a single observation. I'll keep that strictly secondary to the pre-registered 2 sd verdict.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T03:19:42

My script's automated call there was too crude, and the careful reading points the other way. Restricting to the two panels that actually *had* to rotate (A and D started off-target; B and C were already on the commanded director, which inflates their residuals):

| panel | σ/σ_c | started | w(after) | C40 law | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1.49 | 66° → 6° | 0.531 | 0.543 | **−0.011** |
| D | **0.68** | 66° → 6° | 0.567 | 0.357 | **+0.209** |

A sits exactly on the law; D sits 0.21 above it. So D is anomalous — but it *did* end on the commanded director with a +0.338 excess, so I can't dismiss it either. Q23 stays open and needs a write, not more re-analysis.

But the re-analysis suggests something sharper than "is σ_c 302". **σ_c may be an artefact of the threshold I just corrected.** σ_c = 302 was defined as where panels begin clearing the threshold — and that threshold was 3× too high. Lower it correctly and the crossing point moves. C40's *law* (w = 0.234 ln σ − 0.887) is untouched by the correction and describes a perfectly smooth rise with no threshold in it. IT1's panel D switching at 0.68 σ_c is exactly what a smooth law predicts and a hard threshold forbids.

So the real question is whether there is a threshold at all. That's now the load-bearing one, because σ_c is *presupposed by every design I've run* — I pick σ = 2 σ_c because of it. Q21 (where alternation dies) is a good question but changes no other experiment's setup.

I'm building IT5 as a σ ladder on that basis: four panels at 0.4 / 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.5 σ_c, identical period Λ, spacing and density, differing only in dwell, scored against the C45 null. A hard threshold predicts the first two fail; a smooth law predicts all four switch with w rising as ln σ. It's cheap — about 14 minutes of writing — and I'll settle 6 slots for 4 panels so the reference and test arms can be matched on starting dominant, which is the IT4 lesson.

Say the word if you'd rather have the alternation boundary (Q21) first and I'll switch.

                  rng=None, verbose=False):
    """A charge-balanced lattice panel, optionally randomly thinned.

    Sign alternates every `sign_every` rows, so the template period is
    2 * sign_every * sp. Thinning draws equally from the + and - sets, so the
    panel carries exactly zero net DC at any keep_frac - C13 is not negotiable,
    and C34 means the thinning geometry does not matter, so random is the
    simplest defensible choice.

    all-+ then all--, which makes the tip traverse the panel between every pair

    instead of ~28,000 (19 min). Re-ordering changes the visit sequence only -
    the set of sites, their signs and the charge balance are untouched.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T04:07:30

IT6 is audited and ready to launch the moment IT5 releases the lock.

Where things stand at 00:10, against the 08:00 deadline:

**Running.** IT5 (σ ladder) is 20 minutes in and on pace — a frame every ~5.5 min, currently screening candidates. Expected to finish around 00:55: four rungs at 0.41 / 0.68 / 1.02 / 1.49 σ_c, identical in everything but dwell, six slots settled so all four sit on matched starting states, scored against the C45 null.

**Ready.** IT6 is written, audited, and simulated against real frames. Two stages: a charge-balanced ±9 V raster to deplete one triad member and leave a uni-directional background, then U, T and K as masked pulse lattices commanded 60° from whatever background the raster produces. ~19 min raster + ~25 min letters, both under the per-write cap.

Three things the IT6 design work turned up that are worth flagging now:

- **The letter size is forced, not chosen.** The director is only defined over ~4Λ, so no readout window below ~1.2 µm exists and no stroke thinner than that is resolvable at any pixel count. Legibility then needs letter width ≥ 2× stroke and gaps ≥ stroke, so a three-letter word spans ≥ 8× stroke ≈ 9.6 µm. My first attempt — 1.1 µm strokes on 2.0 µm letters — produced illegible blobs, which is what forced me to work this out properly.
- **Write time = Area × σ / V, with the lattice spacing cancelling exactly.** So a coarser lattice buys nothing, and the first attempt couldn't be rescued by thinning it.
- **My cost estimate was wrong and the gate used the estimate.** A masked lattice runs ~1.55× travel overhead, not the 1.35× measured on solid panels, because the tip crosses the letter gaps. Real cost was 28 min against a 24.5 min estimate. Now the gate uses the built trajectory, which exists before anything is sent — same class of error as gating on a proxy.

I also took your terrace observation into IT6: candidates are now ranked by height range rather than taking the first that passes, and the topography under each letter is recorded *before* the write, so if one letter reads weak there's a topographic fact to check rather than a story to invent.

**Drafted.** Both summary documents — [DOC1_process_and_agent.md](DOC1_process_and_agent.md) and [DOC2_switching_rules_and_theory.md](DOC2_switching_rules_and_theory.md) — complete except the IT5 and IT6 result sections. ## assistant — 2026-08-22T04:17:34

Three iterations are now built, audited and simulated against real frames, queued behind IT5:

| | question | design | write |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IT6** | do the rules compose into a device? | ±9 V raster to deplete one director, then U/T/K as masked pulse lattices commanded 60° away | 19 + 25 min |
| **IT7** | lattice axis, or sign boundary? | 2 PAR + 2 PERP — identical sites, σ, axis, command; only the boundary *orientation* rotates 90° | 22 min |
| **IT8** | is strength set by boundary *density*? | `sign_every` 1/2/4/8 at fixed σ — boundary densities 6.7 / 3.3 / 1.7 / 0.8 per µm | 22 min |

IT7 and IT8 both come out of re-reading C46. The re-scored magnitudes order themselves by **sign-boundary count**, not template period — 16 boundaries 7.3×, 4 boundaries 5.7×, 1 boundary 2.5×, zero boundaries nothing — which is a mechanism rather than C41's "the period doesn't matter". IT7 tests whether the boundary *direction* is what the film couples to (this has been confounded in every panel ever written here, since sign has always alternated perpendicular to the command, putting the boundary lines parallel to it). IT8 tests whether the *density* sets the magnitude, with IT3's own numbers as the quantitative target.

I also raised the cumulative write cap from 180 to 330 min, and recorded why in PITFALLS §13 rather than changing it quietly. The justification is two-part and I'd not have done it on one part alone: you asked for the loop to continue, **and** the probe-health signal is measured and flat — tile spread 0.101 → 0.100 → 0.095 → 0.098 across IT1–IT4, with no trend over ~100 min of writing. The minutes cap was only ever a proxy for that, so it's now backed by a real gate (`TILE_SD_MAX = 0.150`, 50 % above the observed band) that stops the loop if the readout actually degrades. The per-iteration 26-min cap stands — nothing about working overnight makes a single long write safer.

IT5 is still running, ~45 min in. Waiting on it before launching IT6.

def dir_state(tag, cx, cy, win_um, triad, cmd_deg=None, folder=None):
    """Population over the triad, the dominant director, and the lead.

    lead = w(commanded) - max(w(other two)). Signed, within-frame, so it is
    comparable across frames of different gain. Returns None if the window is
    too small for dir_power (see window_check).
    """
    w = np.array([sq_power(tag, cx, cy, win_um, t, folder=folder)[0]
                  for t in triad])
    if not np.isfinite(w).all() or w.sum() <= 0:
        return None
    w = w / w.sum()
    dom = float(triad[int(w.argmax())])
    out = dict(w=w, dom=dom, peak=float(sq_power(tag, cx, cy, win_um,
                                                 dom, folder=folder)[1]))
    if cmd_deg is not None:
        ic = int(np.argmin([abs((t - cmd_deg + 90) % 180 - 90) for t in triad]))
        out['lead'] = float(w[ic] - np.delete(w, ic).max())
        out['w_cmd'] = float(w[ic])
        out['on_target'] = bool(int(w.argmax()) == ic and out['lead'] > 0)
    return out

## assistant — 2026-08-22T04:26:14

Everything is staged. Current state at 00:45:

**Running:** IT5, ~55 min in, six frames taken, steady cadence. Its write should start shortly.

**Chained:** IT6 launches automatically when IT5 releases the lock — but only if IT5 actually wrote a trajectory. If it halted before writing, the chain stops and says so rather than launching blind.

**Queued and verified:** IT7 (axis vs boundary) and IT8 (boundary-density ladder), both audited and simulated against real frames.

Four things the offline verification caught in IT6 tonight, none of which would have been visible from reading the code:

- **The raster wasn't charge-balanced.** `gen_center_out_raster` takes its magnitude from `v` and its polarity from `start_sign`, so passing `v = −9` on the second pass left *both* passes at +9 V — mean +7.61, a large DC raster over a 10.6 × 4 µm box, which C13 says re-poles out of plane. Two passes with opposite `start_sign` give mean exactly 0.0000. IT6's own guard would have halted on this, but at 01:00 that would have cost the iteration.
- **The readout would have taken 106 minutes.** `dir_state` costs 1.60 s per call, and the figure map as written was 2738 calls (73 min) with another 1221 in the probe grid (33 min). I tried caching the frame load first — it gave nothing, because the cost is compute inside `sq_power`, not I/O. So I coarsened the grids to ~15 min total rather than writing a second, faster director estimator: this campaign has already lost days to two metrics that were nearly the same, and keeping `dir_state` means the figure and the verdict are literally the same number.
- **The letter geometry was illegible** at my first guess, and the constraints turn out to be tight: stroke ≥ ~4Λ ≈ 1.2 µm (the director is undefined below that, at any pixel count), letter width ≥ 2× stroke, gaps ≥ stroke — so a three-letter word needs ≥ 8× stroke ≈ 9.6 µm. And write time = Area × σ / V with the lattice spacing cancelling exactly, so thinning buys nothing.
- **IT6's notebook cell would have been nearly empty**, since its result has neither a within-frame table nor a panel table. The summary is now built from the result dict itself, so the record can't disagree with the numbers.

Waiting on IT5.

- **IT7 and IT8 had the identical defect** with different keys — `W[k]['mode']`, `W[k]['sign_every']`, `W[k]['bound_per_um']`, all of which live on `panels` rather than on the within-frame dict. Fixed before running.
- **Added a key-consistency check** — compare the literal keys a driver *reads* off a dict against the keys something actually *puts* there. Run across all three drivers it found exactly one problem in exactly the right place.
- **Exercised the verdict blocks** against synthetic results, all 8 outcome branches across IT7 and IT8. This is the test that was missing: the build path has been simulated against real frames since IT4, but the verdict path — the code that runs *last*, after everything expensive is spent — never had been. All three of tonight's "my own patch broke something invisible" faults were in exactly that code.

The underlying reason none of the existing checks caught it: the static audit walks the AST for undefined *names*, and a dict key is a string literal inside a subscript, so `W[k]['sigma']` is syntactically flawless. Recorded as PITFALLS §14.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T05:20:02

Both clean at the new dose: 0.88 σ_c, 14.7 min each (down from 21.7 — a 32% saving), 5.2 V·s per site.

I lowered IT7 and IT8 from 1.3 to 0.9 σ_c on IT5's evidence, and the *scientific* reason matters more than the cost saving. C47 found the response **saturates** at w(cmd) ≈ 0.47 across a 2.2× range in σ. Both queued iterations are difference measurements — PAR vs PERP, and a density ladder — and a saturating observable compresses exactly the differences they're built to detect. If every rung saturates, a genuine density dependence reads as *flat*, which is one of IT8's four pre-registered outcomes and I'd have no way to tell it from the real thing. Running nearer the bottom of the working range leaves headroom for a partial effect to show as partial.

0.9 rather than 0.7 because 0.70 σ_c is the *only* point ever measured that low, and I didn't want the positive control sitting on a single measurement.

IT9 stays at 1.3 σ_c deliberately — a rewrite test needs an unambiguous first write, or "not reversible" gets confounded with "not written firmly enough to begin with".

The sim also caught my own guard rejecting its own setpoint: the floor was `< 0.9 σ_c`, written when the target was 1.3 to catch *budget-driven* weakening, and pulse-count rounding lands at 0.88. Retied it to evidence — 0.65, just below IT5's demonstrated 0.70 — rather than to whatever the current target happens to be.

IT6 continues screening.

IT6 chose (−14, −14) — much flatter than the alternatives, which came in at 105–107 nm of relief. The flatness ranking earned its place. Baselines are being taken now.

**C48 is recorded, and it's the most useful thing to come out of tonight.** The purity ceiling is set by the site *spacing*, not by the charge:

- IT5 varied σ by 2.2× at fixed Λ/2 spacing → final population flat at 0.47 (sd 0.014).
- C39 halved the spacing to Λ/4 → 0.85, and five times more reproducible.

This most likely explains C40 away entirely. That law was fitted across 19 panels at *different spacings*, and σ = V·dwell/spacing² — so spacing and σ were collinear by construction. IT5 broke the collinearity and the σ dependence vanished. The r = +0.974 correlation was probably a spacing law wearing σ's clothes.

The practical consequence is sharp, and it bears on the deliverable you asked for. Write time = Area × σ / V, and **spacing cancels out of that expression**. So a Λ/4 lattice costs the same time as Λ/2 and reaches nearly double the purity — four times the sites at a quarter of the dwell each. IT6's letters are writing at Λ/2 right now, which means they'll land near w ≈ 0.49 rather than ~0.85.

So there's a decision coming when IT6 reports. If the letters read clearly, I'll run IT7 (axis vs boundary) and IT9 (rewrite). If they're faint, the better use of the remaining night is to **rewrite UTK at Λ/4** — same cost, ~1.7× the contrast, a materially better image of the thing you actually asked for. ## assistant — 2026-08-22T05:45:23

I need to correct what I told you a few minutes ago: **a Λ/4 lattice is not free.** I claimed it costs the same time as Λ/2 because write time = Area × σ / V has the spacing cancel out. That identity is right about the *dwell* and wrong about the *trajectory* — travel between sites has a floor, and four times the sites means four times the hops. Measured on the real builder for the UTK mask at Λ = 301 nm:

| spacing | sites | dwell each | dwell total | travel | real total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Λ/2 | 1188 | 0.84 s | 16.6 min | 8.5 min | **25.1 min** |
| Λ/4 | 4756 | 0.20 s | 15.9 min | 18.4 min | **34.3 min** |

The dwell halves agree to 4%, exactly as the identity requires. The travel nearly doubles. So Λ/4 buys ~1.7× purity for ~1.4× time — still a good trade, but it has to be stated honestly, and a Λ/4 UTK exceeds the 26-min per-write cap and would need splitting into two files (U+T, then K).

Both FINDINGS C48 and DOC2 are corrected with the measured table. This is the second time tonight a cost model of mine was wrong in the travel term — the masked-lattice overhead was 1.55× against an assumed 1.35× — so the general lesson is recorded too: an identity that cancels a variable is about the quantity it describes, not about the wall clock.

IT6 is still on baselines; the raster hasn't written yet.

## assistant — 2026-08-22T06:46:51

Two new findings recorded while IT10b runs.

**C49 — the raster reverses sign with poling state.** On virgin film a charge-balanced raster *aligns* the family parallel to its scan lines (0.415 → 0.601); on pre-poled film C26 found it depletes them (0.29 → 0.14 and similar). Five measurements, three one way and two the other, split entirely by poling state — and C26's own unpoled control was already on the virgin side. Practically it's an upgrade: one raster aligns 42 µm² to w = 0.60 in 23.5 min, better purity than a Λ/2 lattice and far more area.

It also opens the sharpest inconsistency in the theory (Q28). Each raster pass is *spatially uniform in sign* — all of pass 1 at +9 V, all of pass 2 at −9 V — so within a pass there are no sign boundaries between adjacent lines. C43 found a spatially uniform-polarity **lattice** does nothing at all. Yet this uniform raster gives the largest alignment in the campaign. Either a continuous sweep couples through something isolated dwells don't, or what matters is the line pattern at Λ/2 pitch rather than the sign pattern.

**C50 — the first retention measurement.** Over 17 minutes with the tip in contact: 0.179 → 0.179, 0.601 → 0.597, 0.220 → 0.223. Largest change 0.004, against a switching threshold of order 0.06–0.10. Every result in this campaign is a before/after comparison that implicitly assumes the written state survives long enough to be read, and that had never been tested. It holds — over 17 minutes, for a raster-aligned state. IT9 is the designed version for lattice-written states.

I've also fixed S9 properly rather than by evasion. IT10b writes deliberately into the area IT6 prepared, so it now **declares** `reuse_areas=['IT6_UTK']` in its proposal; preflight skips exactly those entries and prints that it's an explicit exception. Renaming IT10b to match IT6 would have silenced the guard and made the record show one iteration where there were two.
